# Theming: fonts and colours from a theme

This is the contract for every agent migrating call sites under
`docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.md`. It says what a view writes, what the
tokens are called, and what Ripul's theme document looks like. If you need a
token, role or rule that is not here, ask the foundation owner (the plan's
Foundation section): do not invent one.

Status on 10 October 2026: the document's path and shape below are fixed. The
accessor section is filled in as the foundation lands; a heading marked
"pending" is not yet a contract.

## Ripul's theme document

**Path:** `theme/ripul-theme.json` at the repository root. One file for native
and web. The native app bundles it as `ripul-theme.json`; the web build reads
the same file.

**Shape.** Every key is optional. An absent key means "today's look": the
default written in code on that platform. So the default document is nearly
empty.

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "name": "Ripul",
  "palette": {
    "teal": { "light": "#1f6f70", "dark": "#62b9b4" },
    "ink": "#1b2a41"
  },
  "roles": {
    "ripul.accent": "teal",
    "ripul.text": "system:label"
  },
  "typography": {
    "families": { "text": "system", "display": "system", "code": "system-monospaced" },
    "roles": {
      "eyebrow": { "family": "text", "size": 15, "weight": "semibold",
                   "relativeTo": "subheadline", "tracking": 0, "uppercase": true }
    }
  }
}
```

(The values above show the grammar. They are not the default document, which
sets none of them.)

| Key | Holds |
|---|---|
| `schema` | `1`. A reader ignores keys it does not know |
| `name` | A label for people |
| `palette` | Named colours. Name to a **colour value** |
| `roles` | Colour roles. Role name to a **reference** |
| `typography.families` | The three families: `text`, `display`, `code` |
| `typography.roles` | Type roles. Role name to an object, every field optional |

**Colour value**: a string, or an object `{ "light": <string>, "dark": <string> }`.
Each string is one of:

- `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA` (the `#` is optional);
- `system:<name>`: a platform system colour, live (it follows light, dark and
  increased contrast). The names are listed under "System colour names". The
  web has no system colours: a web reader treats a `system:` value as absent
  and uses its own default for that role.

A light and dark pair exists only in `palette`. This keeps `roles` a flat map
of strings, which is what the theme editor writes.

**Reference** (the value of a role): a string that is, tried in this order,

1. a palette name (`"teal"`),
2. another role's name (`"ripul.accent"`), followed until it ends; a cycle resolves to the role's default,
3. a literal colour string as above (`"#1f6f70"`, `"system:label"`).

**Colour role names** carry the reserved prefix `ripul.` in the document
(`ripul.accent`), because the same names resolve inside another host's theme
document (WAC's), where an unprefixed `accent` is the host's own. The list is
under "Colour roles".

**Families**: `"system"`, `"system-serif"`, `"system-rounded"`,
`"system-monospaced"`, or the name of a font family the app bundles
(`"Archivo"`). The web maps `system` to its present default stack.

**Type role object**:

| Field | Meaning | When absent |
|---|---|---|
| `family` | `text`, `display` or `code` | the role's default family |
| `size` | points at the default Dynamic Type size | the system size of `relativeTo` |
| `weight` | `ultraLight`, `thin`, `light`, `regular`, `medium`, `semibold`, `bold`, `heavy`, `black` | the system weight of `relativeTo` |
| `relativeTo` | the system text style it scales with | the role's default |
| `tracking` | points | 0 |
| `uppercase` | boolean | false |
| `catalystSize` | points on Mac Catalyst, which has no Dynamic Type | `size` |

Type role names have no prefix: the `typography` section belongs to the SDK
alone. The list is under "Type roles".

**In another host's document.** The SDK reads the same three sections from any
host's theme document, using that host's own key names for the palette and
roles (WAC: `colors` and `semantic`). A host that writes none of the `ripul.`
names gets the system look in the SDK's screens.

## Colour roles

| Role | Document name | Default (today's look) | For |
|---|---|---|---|
| `accent` | `ripul.accent` | `system:tint` | Selection, links, primary buttons, the unread mark |
| `onAccent` | `ripul.onAccent` | `#FFFFFF` | Text and icons on an accent fill |
| `canvas` | `ripul.canvas` | `system:systemBackground` | The app's background |
| `surface` | `ripul.surface` | `system:secondarySystemGroupedBackground` | Cards and grouped rows |
| `surfaceSunken` | `ripul.surfaceSunken` | `system:systemGroupedBackground` | The ground behind cards |
| `text` | `ripul.text` | `system:label` | Primary text |
| `textSecondary` | `ripul.textSecondary` | `system:secondaryLabel` | Detail lines |
| `textTertiary` | `ripul.textTertiary` | `system:tertiaryLabel` | Timestamps, hints |
| `textQuaternary` | `ripul.textQuaternary` | `system:quaternaryLabel` | The faintest marks |
| `separator` | `ripul.separator` | `system:separator` | Hairlines |
| `success` | `ripul.success` | `system:systemGreen` | Online, done |
| `warning` | `ripul.warning` | `system:systemOrange` | Waiting, caution |
| `danger` | `ripul.danger` | `system:systemRed` | Errors, destructive actions |
| `info` | `ripul.info` | `system:systemBlue` | A neutral notice that is not the accent |
| `neutral` | `ripul.neutral` | `system:systemGray` | Inactive, disabled, a grey mark |

`textQuaternary`, `info` and `neutral` are additions to the plan's list, made
so that `.quaternary`, a blue that means "information" and `Color.gray` have a
faithful home.

## Type roles

| Role | Default |
|---|---|
| `largeTitle`, `title`, `title2`, `title3`, `headline`, `body`, `callout`, `subheadline`, `footnote`, `caption`, `caption2` | The system text style of the same name, family `text` |
| `display` | `title`, family `display` |
| `eyebrow` | `subheadline`, semibold, family `text` |
| `code` | `body`, family `code` |

## System colour names

`tint`, `label`, `secondaryLabel`, `tertiaryLabel`, `quaternaryLabel`,
`placeholderText`, `separator`, `opaqueSeparator`, `link`,
`systemBackground`, `secondarySystemBackground`, `tertiarySystemBackground`,
`systemGroupedBackground`, `secondarySystemGroupedBackground`,
`tertiarySystemGroupedBackground`, `systemFill`, `secondarySystemFill`,
`tertiarySystemFill`, `quaternarySystemFill`, `systemRed`, `systemOrange`,
`systemYellow`, `systemGreen`, `systemMint`, `systemTeal`, `systemCyan`,
`systemBlue`, `systemIndigo`, `systemPurple`, `systemPink`, `systemBrown`,
`systemGray`, `systemGray2` to `systemGray6`.

## What a view writes (pending)

Filled in when the accessors land.

entries.description:
Discuss an existing comment without changing its status. Use this to
argue a point, ask for clarification, or record why you are about to
accept or decline something.

entries.name: mcp__ripul_tools__planResolve
entries.description:
Move a comment's status.

- **accepted** — you agree the point is valid. The fix is now owed;
  create a task with planTask. A blocking comment that is merely
  accepted still holds the plan open.
- **resolved** — the plan body has actually been changed to address it.
  ENFORCED as the reviewer's confirming verb: a Draft:/Address:-titled
  session is refused `resolved` on comments it did not author — mark
  them `accepted` and the reviewer confirms on their next round.
- **wontfix** — you have considered it and are declining, with a reason
  in `note`.

**Nothing reopens.** `resolved` and `wontfix` are terminal, and this
tool will refuse to move a comment back. That rule is what stops a
multi-round review relitigating points an earlier round settled — if
there is genuinely something new, file a new comment.

Convention: the reviewer who raised a comment is the one who marks it
resolved. The author accepts or declines; the reviewer confirms the fix.

note.description: Why. Required in practice for wontfix — a decline without a reason will just be re-raised.

status.description: The new status. Terminal states cannot be undone.

1	# A theme-aware codebase
2	
3	**Status**: accepted by Peter on 10 October 2026, with every recommendation under "Open questions" taken. Foundation started the same day; a review runs beside it.
4	**Depends on**: the SDK theme engine (shipped, SDK 0.5.10 onward), `ripul-ios-sdk/docs/remote-themes.md`
5	**Reference host**: `WAC_ios_final` (branch `v3`), the one app built on the engine today
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	Ripul's website has a brand: a warm paper canvas, navy ink, a teal accent, Archivo for text and Instrument Serif for headings. Ripul's apps do not carry it. The native screens are stock iOS (system font, system blue), the chat is Material (Roboto, blue `#0078d4`), and the one branded screen, the empty chat, sits between them looking like a page from the website.
10	
11	The cause is not taste, it is plumbing. The SDK has a theme engine, a hosted theme document, an in-app theme editor and a review-and-publish flow. WAC is built on all of it. Ripul's own app uses none of it: every font and colour is written at the call site, so "use teal" or "try Archivo" means editing thousands of lines, and nobody can try a look on a phone before deciding.
12	
13	This plan makes every colour and typeface in the first-party apps come from a theme, without changing how anything looks. A second, small step then applies the brand as a theme document that can be switched on a phone.
14	
15	## What exists today
16	
17	Measured on `main`, 10 October 2026.
18	
19	| Surface | State |
20	|---|---|
21	| SDK theme engine | 19 files, about 6,100 lines: three tiers of colour tokens, named styles, remote document with cache and bundle fallback, editor, review and publish, View Explorer readout, label and tab-title text overrides |
22	| WAC | Registers a vocabulary (`WACThemeSpec.make()`), 47 files and about 220 call sites read tokens, theme document served from `llm-proxy.ripul.io/v1/app-themes/wac-v1` |
23	| Ripul app | Configures the engine only in a UI-test fixture (`iOS/RipulAppApp.swift:289`). `AccentColor` is an empty asset, so the accent is system blue |
24	| SDK's own screens | Read no tokens. One file checks whether a theme exists (`Sessions/RipulSolutionsScreen.swift:389`) |
25	| Web chat | Seven MUI themes and a theming guide, but the themes set no font family (so Roboto), and `src` holds about 2,060 hex literals, 2,000 `rgba(` literals and 790 `fontFamily` values outside the theme files |
26	| Website | The palette and the two faces as CSS variables in `website/public/css/site.css` |
27	
28	Native call sites that set a font or a colour directly:
29	
30	| Directory | Files | Fonts | Named colours | Accent or tint | `.primary`/`.secondary` | System backgrounds |
31	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
32	| `ripul-native-app/iOS` | 131 | 556 | 143 | 83 | 374 | 84 |
33	| `ripul-native-app/Shared` | 86 | 133 | 23 | 9 | 128 | 3 |
34	| `ripul-native-app/macOS` | 125 | 204 | 30 | 18 | 143 | 11 |
35	| `ripul-ios-sdk/Sources/RipulAgent` (all) | 447 | 1,366 | 268 | 186 | 1,042 | 138 |
36	
37	Of the font calls in the iPhone app and SDK, about 1,530 use a text style (`.body`, `.caption`) and about 400 use a fixed size. The first kind can be rewritten by a script, and so can the roughly 1,540 uses of `.primary`, `.secondary` and `.tertiary` (see decision 5). The fixed sizes, the named colours and the backgrounds need a decision each: about 1,100 sites.
38	
39	### Three gaps in the engine
40	
41	The engine was lifted from WAC, and WAC is a light-only UIKit app.
42	
43	1. **No fonts.** The engine resolves colours and style knobs. WAC keeps its font family in its own part of the document and reads it with its own helper (`Font.theme`, `UIFont.themeFontName`).
44	2. **One value per colour.** A primitive is a single hex. There is no light and dark pair and no way to name a system colour. WAC sets `UIUserInterfaceStyle` to `Light`. Ripul follows the system appearance.
45	3. **UIKit only.** `ThemeEngine.swift` is inside `#if os(iOS)` and returns `UIColor`. SwiftUI gets a refresh modifier and a themed text view, but no colour or font a view can read. The SDK also builds for macOS 14, where none of this compiles.
46	
47	A fourth point is structural: the engine holds one vocabulary per process, the host's. The SDK's screens are shown inside WAC as well as inside Ripul, so they cannot read tokens that only Ripul's app registers.
48	
49	## Decisions
50	
51	### 1. The first theme is today's look, exactly
52	
53	The default values of every token are what the code does now: the system font at the system sizes, the system accent, the system backgrounds. A migrated call site therefore renders the same pixels as before. This is what lets many agents land small commits on `main` in any order, and it gives one acceptance test for the whole migration: nothing changed.
54	
55	It needs two things from the engine. A colour must be able to name a system colour (`system:label`, `system:systemBackground`, `system:tint`) and resolve to the live dynamic colour, so light, dark and increased contrast stay exact. A type role whose family is `system` must return the system text style itself (`Font.body`), not a custom font that resembles it. Text colours are the exception to the first: their defaults are SwiftUI's own hierarchical styles, not a system colour, because the system draws `.secondary` differently in a list row and on a material (measured, see decision 5).
56	
57	### 2. The brand is a second document, applied last
58	
59	Teal, Archivo and the serif arrive as a theme document after the migration is done, switchable from the theme editor on a phone. The questions argued in the chat that led to this plan (system font or Archivo, blue or teal, neutral canvas or paper) become settings to look at, not decisions to make first.
60	
61	### 3. A small vocabulary, named for the job
62	
63	Tokens are named for what they are for, never for their value. The list is in "The vocabulary" below. A leaf agent that needs a token the list lacks does not invent one: it asks the foundation owner, who adds it or names the existing one.
64	
65	### 4. The SDK owns a base vocabulary beside the host's
66	
67	The SDK registers its own tokens under a reserved `ripul.` prefix, with defaults in code that give the system look. They resolve in any host, with or without a host theme. Ripul's app supplies a document that overrides them. WAC's vocabulary and document are untouched, and its `Theme.json` stays valid byte for byte.
68	
69	### 5. Shared places before call sites
70	
71	A root modifier, the sheet wrapper (`ripulSheet`), the hosting controllers (24 of them), the glass helpers and the shared row components are fixed first.
72	
73	The foundation measured what a root reaches on 10 October 2026: iOS 17.2 and iOS 27.0, light and dark, in a window, a list row, a sheet, a full-screen cover, a popover and two kinds of hosting controller, reading pixels from each.
74	
75	- **The accent needs no call-site edit.** Setting the window's tint (`UIWindow.tintColor`) reaches `.tint`, `Color.accentColor`, `UIColor.tintColor` and button labels in all seven places. SwiftUI's own `.tint()` at the root does not: `Color.accentColor` stays system blue in sheets, covers and popovers, and nothing follows in a hosting controller. About 280 sites need no edit.
76	- **Text colours need an edit, and the script makes it.** A root `.foregroundStyle` cannot carry them. It changes `.secondary` even when set to today's label colour, because SwiftUI then derives secondary as half the root colour. It recolours button labels. It does not reach hosting controllers. The accessor is instead a style of our own that hands back the system's hierarchical style, so `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))` matches `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` pixel for pixel, including in list rows and on materials, where a plain colour would not. About 1,540 sites, all rewritten by the script with no decision to make.
77	
78	Not measured: alerts, confirmation dialogs, menus and navigation bar titles, which the system draws; a second `UIWindow` (each window the SDK creates needs the tint set); Mac Catalyst; increased contrast.
79	
80	### 6. One document for native and web
81	
82	The chat is a web view inside the native app, so the two must agree. The theme is one JSON document in the repository. The native app bundles it and the web build reads the same file to make the first-party MUI theme. Site-key customers keep their own themes: the first-party theme applies only under the first-party presentation (`config/chatPresentation.ts`).
83	
84	### 7. A check whose count only falls
85	
86	A script counts direct fonts and colours per file and compares with a committed baseline. A count above the baseline fails the build. Agents lower the baseline as they migrate. This stops the tree refilling behind them, and its total is the progress measure. `scripts/check_sheet_sizing.py` is the model: it already runs as a pre-build step.
87	
88	### 8. What is exempt
89	
90	Some colours and sizes are not theme. They stay, marked with `// theme-exempt: <reason>` so the check can count them apart:
91	
92	- SF Symbol sizes. A font on an `Image` is an icon size, not type.
93	- Colours that are data: a provider's or model's colour, a chat's colour, terminal ANSI colours, syntax and diff colours.
94	- Brand marks: the Claude and Codex marks, the wordmark's lime dot.
95	- System materials and glass.
96	- Views that exist only in `#if DEBUG` harnesses.
97	- Customer content: `CmsRender/` in the SDK and `src/cms` on the web follow the customer's portal theme (`CmsPortalTheme`), not Ripul's.
98	
99	## The vocabulary
100	
101	Proposed. F1 fixes the final names in `ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md`, and that file is what leaf agents read.
102	
103	Colour roles, each with a light and a dark value:
104	
105	| Role | Default (today's look) | For |
106	|---|---|---|
107	| `accent` | `system:tint` | Selection, links, primary buttons, the unread mark |
108	| `onAccent` | white | Text and icons on an accent fill |
109	| `canvas` | `system:systemBackground` | The app's background |
110	| `surface` | `system:secondarySystemGroupedBackground` | Cards and grouped rows |
111	| `surfaceSunken` | `system:systemGroupedBackground` | The ground behind cards |
112	| `text` | `.primary`, the system's hierarchical style | Primary text |
113	| `textSecondary` | `.secondary` | Detail lines |
114	| `textTertiary` | `.tertiary` | Timestamps, hints |
115	| `separator` | `system:separator` | Hairlines |
116	| `success` | `system:systemGreen` | Online, done |
117	| `warning` | `system:systemOrange` | Waiting, caution |
118	| `danger` | `system:systemRed` | Errors, destructive actions |

**Reference host**: `WAC_ios_final` (branch `v3`), the one app built on the engine today

## Problem

Ripul's website has a brand: a warm paper canvas, navy ink, a teal accent, Archivo for text and Instrument Serif for headings. Ripul's apps do not carry it. The native screens are stock iOS (system font, system blue), the chat is Material (Roboto, blue `#0078d4`), and the one branded screen, the empty chat, sits between them looking like a page from the website.

Ripul's own app uses none of it: every font and colour is written at the call site, so "use teal" or "try Archivo" means editing thousands of lines, and nobody can try a look on a phone before deciding.

## What exists today

Measured on `main`, 10 October 2026.

| Surface | State |

| SDK's own screens | Read no tokens. One file checks whether a theme exists (`Sessions/RipulSolutionsScreen.swift:389`) |

| Website | The palette and the two faces as CSS variables in `website/public/css/site.css` |

Native call sites that set a font or a colour directly:

| Directory | Files | Fonts | Named colours | Accent or tint | `.primary`/`.secondary` | System backgrounds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ripul-native-app/iOS` | 131 | 556 | 143 | 83 | 374 | 84 |
| `ripul-native-app/Shared` | 86 | 133 | 23 | 9 | 128 | 3 |
| `ripul-native-app/macOS` | 125 | 204 | 30 | 18 | 143 | 11 |
| `ripul-ios-sdk/Sources/RipulAgent` (all) | 447 | 1,366 | 268 | 186 | 1,042 | 138 |

Of the font calls in the iPhone app and SDK, about 1,530 use a text style (`.body`, `.caption`) and about 400 use a fixed size. The first kind can be rewritten by a script, and so can the roughly 1,540 uses of `.primary`, `.secondary` and `.tertiary` (see decision 5). The fixed sizes, the named colours and the backgrounds need a decision each: about 1,100 sites.

The engine was lifted from WAC, and WAC is a light-only UIKit app.

2. **One value per colour.** A primitive is a single hex. There is no light and dark pair and no way to name a system colour. WAC sets `UIUserInterfaceStyle` to `Light`. Ripul follows the system appearance.

### 1. The first theme is today's look, exactly

The questions argued in the chat that led to this plan (system font or Archivo, blue or teal, neutral canvas or paper) become settings to look at, not decisions to make first.

Tokens are named for what they are for, never for their value. The list is in "The vocabulary" below. A leaf agent that needs a token the list lacks does not invent one: it asks the foundation owner, who adds it or names the existing one.

The SDK registers its own tokens under a reserved `ripul.` prefix, with defaults in code that give the system look. They resolve in any host, with or without a host theme. Ripul's app supplies a document that overrides them. WAC's vocabulary and document are untouched, and its `Theme.json` stays valid byte for byte.

### 5. Shared places before call sites

A root modifier, the sheet wrapper (`ripulSheet`), the hosting controllers (24 of them), the glass helpers and the shared row components are fixed first.

The foundation measured what a root reaches on 10 October 2026: iOS 17.2 and iOS 27.0, light and dark, in a window, a list row, a sheet, a full-screen cover, a popover and two kinds of hosting controller, reading pixels from each.

- **The accent needs no call-site edit.** Setting the window's tint (`UIWindow.tintColor`) reaches `.tint`, `Color.accentColor`, `UIColor.tintColor` and button labels in all seven places. SwiftUI's own `.tint()` at the root does not: `Color.accentColor` stays system blue in sheets, covers and popovers, and nothing follows in a hosting controller. About 280 sites need no edit.
- **Text colours need an edit, and the script makes it.** A root `.foregroundStyle` cannot carry them. It changes `.secondary` even when set to today's label colour, because SwiftUI then derives secondary as half the root colour. It recolours button labels. It does not reach hosting controllers. The accessor is instead a style of our own that hands back the system's hierarchical style, so `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))` matches `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` pixel for pixel, including in list rows and on materials, where a plain colour would not. About 1,540 sites, all rewritten by the script with no decision to make.

Not measured: alerts, confirmation dialogs, menus and navigation bar titles, which the system draws; a second `UIWindow` (each window the SDK creates needs the tint set); Mac Catalyst; increased contrast.

### 6. One document for native and web

The chat is a web view inside the native app, so the two must agree. The theme is one JSON document in the repository. The native app bundles it and the web build reads the same file to make the first-party MUI theme. Site-key customers keep their own themes: the first-party theme applies only under the first-party presentation (`config/chatPresentation.ts`).

### 7. A check whose count only falls

A script counts direct fonts and colours per file and compares with a committed baseline. A count above the baseline fails the build. Agents lower the baseline as they migrate. - SF Symbol sizes. A font on an `Image` is an icon size, not type.
- Colours that are data: a provider's or model's colour, a chat's colour, terminal ANSI colours, syntax and diff colours.
- Brand marks: the Claude and Codex marks, the wordmark's lime dot.
- System materials and glass.
- Views that exist only in `#if DEBUG` harnesses.

input.message:
From the plan's author. The review is in: 15 comments, 3 blocking, all accepted. The plan is revised (commits 78ac48ae9 and 4f3b9e2f5) and several changes land on your work. Read `docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.review.md` for the reviewer's evidence, and the revised Decisions 1, 4, 5 and 7, The vocabulary, Foundation and Rules. In short:

THREE THINGS OWED BEFORE THE FIRST STREAM CAN START (each has a plan task in your name)
1. Live repaint (t_c8ab26609098). A view already on screen must change when a document is adopted, with nothing written in the view. The SDK's present rule is the opposite: a view repaints only if its body reads `ripulThemeVersion` (ThemeInstrumentation.swift:122-180), and a static accessor bakes its value in. Pick the mechanism and prove it: a `Text` already drawn changes font and colour after `adopt()` with no navigation, in a window, a list row, a sheet and a hosting controller. Candidates in the order I would try: accessors read an `@Observable` store so SwiftUI tracks the read in each body (the SDK's floor is iOS 17); colours as a ShapeStyle reading the environment; the root rebuilds the tree under a new identity (reaches everything, loses navigation, scroll and focus). Whichever wins, an accessor's result must not be kept in a `static let` or stored property, and the check should flag one that is.
2. The wider root measurement (t_23e84f9917a8): your F3 harness again for a material, `.glassEffect`, a selected list row, inside a prominent button, a small bordered button, a section header, navigation title and back button, toolbar items, a tab bar, alerts and confirmation dialogs, menus, swipe actions, a search field, a text field's cursor and selection, a toggle's on colour, and a UIViewRepresentable. Also: the root sets a font only when the document names a non-system family, because a root `.font(.body)` replaces the absent font that small controls and section headers rely on.
3. The compile commands (t_d25b4f28ff28). `swift build` on the host compiles 151 iOS-only SDK files to nothing. Prove on one migrated file, and write into theming.md, the iOS-simulator `swift build` (the form in CLAUDE.md, with `-target arm64-apple-ios17.0-simulator`) and an `xcodebuild build` of RipulApp for the simulator into a /tmp DerivedData with no install.

DECISIONS THAT CHANGE WHAT YOU HAVE WRITTEN
- Another host's document: Ripul's part goes under ONE reserved top-level key, `ripul`, never inside the host's own palette or roles maps. Checked by the reviewer: a light/dark pair under WAC's `colors` makes the decoder in every installed WAC build throw (ThemeEngine.swift:107), after which its remote client keeps the last good theme and updates stop; and unregistered keys show in WAC's editor as custom labels (line 783). So the paragraph "In another host's document" in theming.md needs to change. Ripul's own document may keep the flat form. The base vocabulary lives in a table `configure(_:)` does not clear and a host's editor does not list.
- Pairs sit in a field of their own so the public `primitives` map stays strings. An unresolvable reference falls back to the role's default in code, never magenta. An unknown schema number keeps the last good document.
- Resolve the whole vocabulary once per theme change into an immutable table the accessors read: they run in every session-list row and may be called off the main thread.
- theming.md gets a closed mapping table: for each literal a leaf agent meets, the one role whose default is exactly that value, or "exempt". Where no role fits, a system form through the accessor (proposed `Color.ripul(system: .secondarySystemBackground)`), counted apart. You decide which literals earn a role.
- Accessors take a family argument (216 monospaced sites need `.caption` and fixed sizes in the code family). A fixed size stays fixed in a custom family (`Font.custom(_:fixedSize:)`). Uppercase is not part of a type role: the call site keeps `.textCase`.
- F2's equality test resolves each colour role under light, dark, increased contrast and elevated.
- F4: the theme editor flattens a pair to one hex and cannot pick a system colour or a font (ThemeTokenScreens.swift:361). content.text:
The review is back and it found real problems, so the migration streams are on hold until the foundation proves three things. The plan now shows as Open, which is the honest state.

The reviewer filed 15 comments, including 3 from the web agent. I accepted all of them, revised the plan, and recorded my answer on each. The three blocking ones:

- **Live repaint was undesigned.** As the SDK works today, a screen already drawn would not change when a new theme is loaded. That would break "switch it on your phone". The foundation must now pick a mechanism and prove it on a drawn screen before any stream starts.
- **The compile check I prescribed was empty.** It built the SDK for the Mac, which skips 151 iOS-only files holding about half the font calls. Agents would have pushed uncompiled Swift to `main`. Streams now compile for the iOS simulator before every push.
- **The root-modifier test list was too short.** The first measurement covered seven places. It now has to cover glass, selected rows, prominent buttons, alerts, menus, toolbars and more before streams rely on it.

Changes you would notice:

- **Trying a look is by switcher first, not the theme editor.** The editor writes one colour over a light and dark pair and cannot pick fonts. The foundation adds a switcher between bundled themes; teaching the editor the new shapes moves to the brand step.
- **One more stream.** For the chat to follow a theme switched on the phone, the app has to pass the theme to the web view at run time. That was missing.
- **WAC is protected.** Putting Ripul's colours inside WAC's own colour map would have stopped theme updates in every installed WAC build. Ripul's part now sits under its own reserved key.
- **Other agents are not blocked.** The new check warns until a stream is finished, and only then fails builds.
- **Widgets and the Live Activity wait for the brand step.** Their target does not link the SDK.

Both foundation agents are still running and have been told what changed for them. The reviewer is doing a second pass on my revisions. The SDK agent's job has grown, so I've offered to split the check and the reference screens off to another agent once the accessor names are fixed.

content.content:
===== c_9e679809aca6 should-fix 5-shared-places-before-call-sites
Round 2. "About 1,540 sites, all rewritten by the script with no decision to make" is true for the common form only. Counted in the SDK, iOS and Shared:

- 1,151 are foregroundStyle with .primary, .secondary, .tertiary or .quaternary. These take any style, so the new style drops in.
- 79 are foregroundColor(.primary) or (.secondary). That parameter is a Color, not a style. The script must also change the modifier to foregroundStyle, or a Color form of the text roles must exist.
- 108 write Color.primary or Color.secondary explicitly, often where only a Color is accepted: a shadow, a stroke with opacity, a stored Color property, a function argument. These need a Color form (Color.ripul(.textSecondary) returning Color.secondary by default).
- 53 are a choice between a colour and a hierarchical style in one expression (condition ? Color.accentColor : .secondary, and the like). After the rewrite the two sides are different types and will not compile. They need either the Color form on both sides or a type-erased style. A script can find them; a person or agent has to choose.
- 5 sites use a fixed label colour as a Color (Color(.secondaryLabel) and similar) and 7 more in UIKit. These are not hierarchical: they do not get vibrancy and do not flip in a selected row. The closed table must send them to the system form, never to a text role, or the migration changes pixels on a material.

Why it matters: F2 says text roles are a style and not a Color, and the plan's table shows only the first form. An agent meeting the other 245 sites has no rule, and the 53 mixed ones fail to compile after the script runs.

Proposed fix: say in F2 that each text role has both a style form and a Color form with the same default as today's Color.primary and Color.secondary; have the script rewrite foregroundColor to foregroundStyle only where the argument is a bare hierarchical name; have it leave mixed expressions untouched and list them for the stream's agent; and add the fixed label colours to the closed table as system-form rows.

== F on the wider measurement
From the foundation agent. The wider measurement, as far as I took it. Measured unless marked; the full text is in theming.md, "What the root reaches".

Identity of the style form against the system style, side by side over one uniform colour, default theme, iOS 27.0, light and dark, for .primary, .secondary, .tertiary, .quaternary and .red against .ripul(.text) and its siblings and .ripul(.danger): identical on a plain background, in a list row, a section header, a sheet, inside a prominent button, inside a small bordered button, on .glassEffect(.regular) and on .glassEffect(.clear). On .regularMaterial and .ultraThinMaterial they agree to within 1 in one channel, and two squares of the very same Color.secondary differ by the same amount there, so that is the material and not the accessor. My first attempt put stripes behind the glass and showed large differences; that was the two squares sitting over different stripes, and I discarded it.

The same run showed why the form matters: the .secondary style and Color.secondary draw differently in a list row (128,128,128 against 138,138,142), a prominent button (128,195,255 against 36,90,142), a small bordered button and a section header. So foregroundColor must stay foregroundColor (its argument is a Color), and Color.secondary must become the Color form. See my reply on c_9e679809aca6.

System controls under a themed accent and a themed family, looked at in two screenshots, not sampled: toolbar buttons, a toggle's on colour (it took the accent, it was not green), plain, bordered and prominent buttons, a menu's label, a progress bar, a slider, a label's symbol, the selected tab and an alert's two buttons all took the accent. The family reached form rows, buttons, menus and toolbar buttons. It did not reach a large navigation title, a segmented picker's labels, tab bar labels, or an alert's title and buttons.

Not done from your list: a selected sidebar row (iPad and Catalyst only; I ran on an iPhone), context menus, swipe actions, a search field, a text field's cursor and selection, a second window or scene, a UIViewRepresentable beyond the one in the repaint proof, Mac Catalyst, and iOS 17 for this second run. The root file sets the tint on whichever window it is in, so the Image window group gets it by having the root; I did not measure that.
== theming.md: Limits
## Limits

- **The theme editor cannot edit these tokens.** It writes one hex over a
  pair and cannot choose a system colour or a font. A look is tried by
  loading a document. There is no list of documents in the app's settings:
  the switch is the launch argument and the URL above.
- **The widgets and the Live Activity** do not link the SDK and are not
  themed.
- **A custom family and Dynamic Type.** A themed role with a size uses
  `Font.custom(_:size:relativeTo:)`, which scales on a slightly different
  curve from the system's at accessibility sizes.
- **Mac Catalyst**: `catalystSize` is read; nothing about Catalyst was
  measured, and the reference screens do not capture it.
- **Reference screens** cover what a signed-out install can show: the start
  chooser, the standalone workspace and nine developer fixtures. No session
  list, chat or settings screen is in them, because nothing loads fixture
  data for those. Reduce Motion is not set.

464	## Checking your work
465	
466	All from the repository root.
467	
468	**1. Rewrite the mechanical cases.**
469	
470	```bash
471	python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/rewrite_theme_tokens.py --dry-run <file or directory>
472	python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/rewrite_theme_tokens.py <file or directory>
473	```
474	
475	It rewrites text-style fonts with their weight and chained calls, the
476	monospaced forms, fixed sizes whose view it can see is a `Text` or an
477	`Image`, and the hierarchy styles in both forms. It leaves named colours,
478	mixed ternaries and fixed sizes it cannot place. Its output over the whole
479	SDK (1,814 lines) compiles for iOS and macOS.
480	
481	**2. Do the rest by the closed table.**
482	
483	**3. Lint the diff.**
484	
485	```bash
486	python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/rewrite_theme_tokens.py --lint                 # working tree against HEAD
487	python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/rewrite_theme_tokens.py --lint HEAD~3          # a range
488	python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/rewrite_theme_tokens.py --lint HEAD -- <path>  # some paths
489	```
490	
491	It pairs each removed line with the line that replaced it and accepts the
492	pair only if every token's default is the value it replaced. It reads a hunk
493	that removes and adds the same number of lines; where the counts differ it
494	asks you to pair the lines by hand or mark them.
495	
496	**4. Compile, before every push.**
497	
498	```bash
499	# SDK streams: for the iOS simulator. About 40 s after the first build.
500	cd ripul-ios-sdk && swift build --scratch-path /tmp/ripul-theme-<stream> \
501	  --triple arm64-apple-ios17.0-simulator --sdk "$(xcrun --sdk iphonesimulator --show-sdk-path)"
502	
503	# and once at the end of the stream for macOS:
504	cd ripul-ios-sdk && swift build --scratch-path /tmp/ripul-theme-<stream>-mac
505	```
506	
507	Do not use `-Xswiftc -sdk -Xswiftc ... -Xswiftc -target ...`: that form
508	builds for macOS whatever it is given. Measured: with a type error placed
509	inside `#if os(iOS)` it printed "Build complete", and the `--triple` form
510	reported the error. 151 of the SDK's files are iOS-only.

513

516	  xcodebuild build -project RipulNativeApp.xcodeproj -scheme RipulApp -configuration Debug \
517	  -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' ARCHS=arm64 ONLY_ACTIVE_ARCH=NO \
518	  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO -derivedDataPath /tmp/ripul-theme-<stream>-dd
519	```
520	
521	Measured on this Mac on 10 October 2026: 83 seconds the first time into an
522	empty DerivedData, 8 seconds with nothing changed. It runs the app's
523	pre-build steps, the check among them. It reads the generated project: a
524	stream that adds or removes no file does not run `xcodegen`. One of those
525	pre-build steps builds the standalone web interface into the repository's own
526	folder, so two app builds at the same moment write the same files (reasoned,
527	not tried): if a build fails there, run it again.

- **Web foundation: landed and live.** Three font families in the theme, a first-party theme built from the shared document, the literals check and the style snapshot. The live build's snapshot is identical to the one from before the change.
- **The three blockers are proved by measurement:**

content.content:
--- 77
In another host's document, Ripul's part lives under one reserved top-level key, `ripul`, holding its own palette, roles and typography. It never goes inside the host's own palette or roles maps, for two reasons the review checked in code. A light and dark pair inside WAC's `colors` makes the decoder in every installed WAC build throw (`ThemeEngine.swift:107` reads that map as strings), after which the remote client keeps its last good theme and updates stop. And keys the host did not register show in the host's theme editor as custom labels (`ThemeEngine.swift:783`). An older build ignores a top-level key it does not know. Ripul's own document may use the flat form.
--- 88
- **Text colours need an edit, and the script makes it.** A root `.foregroundStyle` cannot carry them. It changes `.secondary` even when set to today's label colour, because SwiftUI then derives secondary as half the root colour. It recolours button labels. It does not reach hosting controllers. The accessor is instead a style of our own that hands back the system's hierarchical style, so `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))` matches `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` pixel for pixel, including in list rows and on materials, where a plain colour would not. About 1,540 sites, all rewritten by the script with no decision to make.
--- 187
**F4. Ripul's document.** One JSON file at a path both builds can read, registered by the app at launch. Proposed path: `theme/ripul-theme.json` at the repository root. The foundation agent confirms the path and writes it and the document's shape into `theming.md` before the engine work, because W1 reads both. With the default values it is nearly empty. The theme editor cannot yet edit what this plan adds: it writes a single hex over a light and dark pair, and has no way to choose a system colour or a font (`ThemeTokenScreens.swift:361`). So a look is tried by loading a document, not by editing one. The foundation adds a switcher that lists the bundled documents: the default, the loud test document, and later the brand. Until the editor learns the new shapes (a separate task), it does not offer Ripul's roles for editing.
--- 214

--- 222
| B1 | The handoff of the theme document from the native shell to the web view: the bridge in the SDK, the theme provider on the web | | |
--- 244
S1 goes first among the native streams: it holds the session list and the rows, the screens this plan started from, and it will find the gaps in the accessors while only one agent is affected. S1 also measures the session list's scroll before and after, with a control, since an accessor now runs in every row.
--- 257
6. Run the check and the mapping lint on its files, then lower its own baseline. Commit.
--- 281
  - SDK streams compile for the iOS simulator, not the host. 151 of the SDK's files are iOS-only, and a macOS build compiles them to nothing and reports success. `swift build --scratch-path /tmp/ripul-theme-<stream> -Xswiftc -sdk -Xswiftc $(xcrun --sdk iphonesimulator --show-sdk-path) -Xswiftc -target -Xswiftc arm64-apple-ios17.0-simulator`, and once for macOS at the end of the stream.
--- 325
- `ripul-native-app/CatalystWindowControls`, `device-runner`, `UITests`, `experiments` and `support-probe`. CarPlay, whose templates the system draws.

input.message:
From the plan's author. A third round, please, and this one decides whether the first migration stream may start.

WHAT HAS HAPPENED SINCE YOUR SECOND ROUND
- Both foundations have landed and their tasks are marked done. The foundation agent replied on each of your three blocking comments with what it measured (read docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.review.md), and the contract in ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md has nothing marked pending.
- I accepted your four second-round comments and revised the plan (commit 34f2af285); each has a note.
- The compile finding was worse than either of us wrote: the command you proposed and I put in the plan builds for macOS whatever it is given. The foundation agent measured that, and I checked it myself in a throwaway package with a type error planted inside an iOS-only branch: both -Xswiftc forms print "Build complete", and the --triple form reports the error. The plan's Rules, theming.md and CLAUDE.md (commit 2117edf1e) now give the --triple form.

WHAT I NEED
1. For each of the three blocking comments (c_90fc0a136c49 live repaint, c_11648330ac1b the root and its measurement, c_27785d19be30 the compile check): judge the reported proof against the code and the contract, not against my summary. Resolve it if the proof is real and sufficient for the first stream to start. If it is not, reply with what is missing and leave it.
2. Two things I want your judgement on in particular, because I am not sure they should hold the first stream:
   - The wider measurement did not run a selected sidebar row, context menus, swipe actions, a search field, a text cursor, a second window, or anything on Mac Catalyst. The plan now says those rest on the accessor tests under the default document and are measured before the brand step, Catalyst first. Is that the right place to draw the line?
   - The reference screens cover only what a signed-out install shows. No session list, chat or Settings screen is in them. The plan now makes a session-list fixture the first job of the first stream. Is that enough, or should the fixture exist before the stream is started at all?
3. Confirm or leave the other accepted comments as before, and file anything new.

Please keep the reply short: for each blocking comment, resolved or not and the one reason; then anything new.

## The three blocking comments

- **`c_90fc0a136c49` (live repaint): resolved.** The mechanism is in the code and reads correctly: every accessor reads the `@Observable` store through `RipulTheme.table`, the colour style carries its resolved value, and the table is swapped under a lock. A plain SwiftUI view needs nothing written in it.
- **`c_11648330ac1b` (the root): resolved.** The style form is measured against the system style in the contexts where the default document is at risk, and the root applies nothing under the default document (`testTheRootAppliesNothingWithNoTheme`).
- **`c_27785d19be30` (compile check): resolved.** I reran it in a throwaway package: the `-Xswiftc` form I proposed in round one prints "Build complete" over a type error in an iOS-only branch, and the `--triple` form fails on it. The command I gave was wrong; the one now in the plan, `theming.md` and `CLAUDE.md` is right.

## Your two questions

- **The unmeasured list: right line, with one exception.** Context menus, swipe actions, a search field, the text cursor and a second window only matter once a document sets an accent or family, so before the brand step is correct. The selected sidebar row on Catalyst is different: it is a default-document question, and the session list is that sidebar. It should be part of the first stream's first job. It does not hold the start.
- **The fixture: enough as the first stream's first job, on one condition.** The fixture and its baseline must be committed before the rewrite script runs over `Sessions/`, or the baseline compares the migration with itself. The plan does not say that yet.

## Other accepted comments

Resolved: `c_9e679809aca6`, `c_ff04143f266a`, `c_f5460988f7ee`, `c_333b7f662bca`. One claim under `c_f5460988f7ee` is still reasoned, not run: that SDK 0.7.169 decodes a document carrying the `ripul` key. The web foundation agent's three comments are left for that agent to confirm.

## New (both should-fix, neither holds the first stream)

- **`c_6ed44ea7f767` (Workstreams):** the two conditions above. It also asks Verification to say that the glass helpers and sheet wrapper were migrated before any session-list baseline existed, so their proof is the lint and the accessor tests only.
- **`c_0725e81bc7bf` (Foundation):**
  - The repaint proof ran in a probe under `/tmp` and nothing in the repository would fail if the store read moved back into `resolve`. Commit it as a test.
  - The store's `revision` integer is read off the main thread unguarded.
  - Several app builds at once is untried, and a collision in the standalone pre-build step can pass with half-written output. Give the compile-check build a way to skip that step, and time two builds together before the parallel streams start.","status":"completed"}

input.task:
You are the first migration stream, S1, of the plan at docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.md in this repository: move every font and colour in `ripul-ios-sdk/Sources/RipulAgent/Sessions/` (82 files: the session list, its rows, the machine rows, the new-chat sheets) onto the theme accessors, with no visible change. Peter accepted the plan, it has been through three review rounds and is locked, and the foundation you build on landed today.

READ FIRST
- The plan, whole. Then `ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md`, whole: it is the contract (what a view writes, the closed table, the commands under "Checking your work", the limits). Where it and the plan differ, theming.md is right.
- ripul_guide topics `plans`, `trains` and `devices`.
- Your plan tasks: t_6d054262df49 (the fixture, your first job) and t_b8c086bc68cb (the migration, already marked doing). Mark each done with planTaskStatus and put your report in the note: the host can lose a reply when it reloads, and the plan's log is what survives.

WHY YOU GO ALONE
You are the one stream running, so that gaps in the accessors, the closed table, the rewrite script, the lint and the check are found while one agent is affected and not nine. So do not work around a gap. If the table has no row for a literal you meet, the script mangles a form, the lint rejects a faithful pair, or an accessor is missing: stop on that site, file a planComment on the plan's Foundation section, and tell the foundation agent (list_agents; it is the chat that carried out "the Foundation section (F1 to F6)", agentId cli_79a0ef34-552a-4824-895c-9c4d26c71963). Carry on with the sites that are not affected. A list of what you had to ask for is one of the most useful things you will hand back.

ORDER
1. The fixture, before anything in `Sessions/` is migrated. The reference screens the foundation built cover only what a signed-out install shows; nothing loads fixture data for a session list. Build a way to show the session list with fixed data in a Debug build with no account: machines online and offline, and sessions that between them show every state a row can draw (unread, pinned, selected, a tool running with its label under the icon, each provider, a long title that truncates, the lozenge presentation). Look at how the existing launch-argument harnesses do it (`ripul-native-app/iOS/RipulAppApp.swift`, the `RipulUITest…` arguments; the UI tests in `ripul-native-app/UITests`). Add it to `ripul-native-app/scripts/theme_reference_screens.py` and capture the baseline. The fixture must be committed and its baseline captured BEFORE the rewrite script touches `Sessions/`: a baseline taken afterwards compares the migration with itself. For this job only you may edit outside your files (the harness hook in the app, the reference-screens script): no other stream has started. Say exactly what you touched.
2. In the same first job, measure a selected sidebar row on Mac Catalyst under the default document: does the style form (`.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))`) draw the same pixels as `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` in a selected row? The session list is that sidebar, and nothing has been measured on Catalyst yet. Do this in a throwaway probe app under /tmp built for Mac Catalyst (the foundation's probe is at /tmp/theme-f3 if it is still there). Do NOT quit, replace or relaunch the Ripul Catalyst app that is running on this Mac: it is Peter's.
3. Measure the session list's scroll before you migrate, in a way you can repeat afterwards, with a control. An accessor will run in every row. Peter tests scroll with nothing streaming, and wants measured before-and-after figures, not impressions.
4. Migrate, following "Checking your work" in theming.md step by step: the rewrite script (dry run first), the rest by the closed table, the lint, the compile for the iOS simulator before EVERY push (the `--triple` form; the `-Xswiftc -sdk` form builds for macOS whatever it is given), the check on your paths, then `--update S1`. Small commits, pushed at once.
5. At the end: the macOS build of the SDK, the reference screens against your baseline, the scroll measurement again, then `--finish S1`. `--finish` refuses while anything is left in your files, other agents' additions included: clear those too.
6. When S1 is finished, add the short rule the plan describes to CLAUDE.md beside the sheet rule (task t_6c69d5023a99): fonts and colours come from the accessors, with a pointer to theming.md and the command that runs the check on a list of paths.

RULES
- Edit only files in `Sessions/`, apart from the exceptions in step 1 and step 6. The foundation's own files are off limits whatever their names: the `Theme*.swift` files, `ThemeCore/`, `SheetPresentation.swift`, `GlassModifiers.swift`, `GlassButton.swift`, `GlassMastheadView.swift`, `GlassTopBar.swift`, and theming.md.
- No visual change. Map faithfully by the closed table: never choose a role whose default differs from the literal it replaces. Where the faithful result looks wrong, keep it faithful and list it for the brand step. Two are already known: the tool label under a row's icon is fixed at 8 points (`UnifiedSessionRow.swift` near line 397), and the model name in each row is drawn in the provider's colour.
- A provider's or model's colour and a chat's colour are data, not theme: exempt them with the marker theming.md gives.
- The 53-odd expressions that choose between a colour and a hierarchy style are left by the script and are yours to decide; keep each side drawing what it draws today.
- Several other sessions are working on `main` in this repository. Unrelated files will appear in git status: leave them, add your own by explicit path, never stash or reset.
- Simulators are borrowed from Trainyard's pool (CLAUDE.md says how). The simulator train is for the reference screens only. Do not install to Peter's iPhone.

YOUR FINAL REPLY, AND THE SAME IN THE TASK NOTES
- The commits, and the check's count for S1 before and after.
- What the fixture is and how to launch it; where the baseline is.
- The Catalyst result, with what you ran.
- The scroll figures before and after, with the control.
- The reference-screen difference.
- Every gap you found in the accessors, the table, the script, the lint or the check, and what became of each.
- What the next streams (the rest of the SDK, then the app) should know before they start.
- For each claim, whether you ran it or reasoned it.

You are the first web migration stream, W2, of the plan at docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.md in this repository: move every colour and typeface literal in `chrome-extension/src/logging/components/chat/` onto the theme, with no visible change. Peter accepted the plan, it has been through three review rounds and is locked, and the web foundation you build on (W1) landed today and is live.

READ FIRST
- The plan, whole; the web parts are Decision 6, the W1 list under Foundation, the web rows and paragraphs under Workstreams, Rules and Verification.
- `chrome-extension/docs/features/ui/themingGuide.md`, whole: W1 wrote how a component reads the three families and the first-party theme, how to run the literals check and the snapshot, and the mapping from each role to an MUI token.
- The scripts W1 added in `chrome-extension/scripts/`: `check-theme-literals.mjs`, `theme-snapshot.mjs`, `theme-first-party-scope.mjs`, and their baseline and scope files.
- `.ripul/memories/` (start at MEMORY.md): there is a memory from today on the URL that renders the first-party chat in a clean headless WebKit.
- ripul_guide topics `plans`, `trains` and `browser`.
- Your plan tasks: t_0efc57636e5c (the fixture chat, your first job) and t_fb5cba995cd5 (the migration). Mark t_fb5cba995cd5 doing when you start it, and mark each done with planTaskStatus with your report in the note: the host can lose a reply when it reloads, and the plan's log is what survives.

ORDER
1. The fixture chat, before any file is migrated. Today the snapshot can only reach an empty chat, because a clean browser has no chat with messages in it and nothing in the app loads one. So nothing in a message row can be shown to be unchanged. Build a fixture chat for the first-party presentation: a fixed set of messages and actions that between them draw each thing the chat can show (a user message, assistant text with markdown and a code block, a thinking block, each kind of tool row and panel, a question, an error, the composer in its states), loaded behind a URL flag, with no account and no network. Add it to the pages in `theme-snapshot.mjs` and capture a new baseline. The fixture must be deployed and its baseline captured BEFORE you migrate anything: a baseline taken afterwards compares the migration with itself. The panels stream (W3, `src/logging/panels/`) waits for this fixture, so say in your report how it uses it.
2. Migrate `src/logging/components/chat/`: hex and rgba literals become theme tokens as the guide says (`alpha()` of a palette value for a translucent colour, never a string token passed to `alpha()`), and font families become the theme's `text`, `display` or `code` family. Remove a family only when the snapshot shows the same face before and after: inheriting is not the text family, because the page body is `sans-serif` and only MUI's own components draw in Roboto.
3. Run the literals check and lower your own baseline as you go; compare the snapshot against your baseline after each batch; finish the stream in the check when your count is zero.

THINGS I KNOW ABOUT YOUR FILES
- `v2/V2StarterScreen.tsx` (the empty chat) declares its own `@font-face` for Instrument Serif and its own palette of four accents, light and dark. Faithful means those values move into the theme and the screen reads them from there; they do not change. Making the four accents one is a later, separate step.
- `ChatInputContainer.tsx` (the composer) has literal fallbacks beside theme reads, and a hard-coded purple.
- Syntax and diff colours, and a model's or persona's colour, are data, not theme: exempt them the way the guide says.
- Everything you do applies under the first-party presentation only (`src/config/chatPresentation.ts`, gated in `src/context/FeatureScopeContext.tsx`). Site-key customers must see no change, and the first-party theme must stay ahead of a learned site-key theme, which W1 arranged.

RULES
- Edit only files in `src/logging/components/chat/`, plus what the fixture and the snapshot need (say exactly what you touched outside your directory). `src/themes/ThemeProvider.tsx`, `src/themes/firstPartyTheme.ts` and `src/hosted-app/NativeBridge.ts` belong to another stream that has not started: if you need a change there, file a planComment on the plan's Workstreams section and tell me.
- No visible change. Where the faithful result looks wrong, keep it faithful and list it for the brand step.
- `npx tsgo --noEmit` after every change. `data-ui` on anything you add. Deploy only through `npm run deploy:all` (the web train), from a committed and pushed tree, and take a hold while you compare snapshots against the live build.
- If a role, a family or a mapping you need is missing, do not invent one: file a planComment on Workstreams and ask the web foundation agent (list_agents; the chat that carried out "the web foundation (W1)", agentId cli_d8cf1a60-5f7c-4292-8a88-7092a4831f28). A list of what you had to ask for is one of the most useful things you will hand back.
- Several other sessions are working on `main` in this repository. Unrelated files will appear in git status: leave them, add your own by explicit path, never stash or reset.

YOUR FINAL REPLY, AND THE SAME IN THE TASK NOTES
- The commits, what was deployed, and the check's count for your stream before and after.
- What the fixture is, how to load it, what it covers and what it cannot.
- The snapshot difference.
- Every gap you found in the theme, the check or the snapshot, and what became of each.
- What W3 (the panels) and W4 (the other first-party files) should know before they start.
- For each claim, whether you ran it or reasoned it.
