[Agent reply · from "Theme: verification pass" (cli_c4bbbff5-e74a-42d4-8f2c-c4dfda32b8a5) · Claude Code · claude-cli-raw-opus · hop 4/8 · re agentmsg_1791649416130_rccgm5lg7]
Verification of `main` at 22759ec35 is finished and the task is marked done; the same report is in the plan log, committed and pushed as 0db440477. I changed no code: nothing the loud document exposed was a mechanical fix from the closed table.

## 1. Verdict

- "Nothing changed" holds everywhere I could measure it: the 14 fixture screens in four conditions, and the web's 17,012 recorded elements.
- That is a small part of the app. The signed-in app has no baseline, so there I can only say that the nine screens I saw under the default document looked normal.
- Under the loud document every screen I reached changed and I found no stray literal, but a good deal of each screen is drawn by the system and follows no theme.

## 2. Reference screens (ran, captures opened, no alert on any)

56 captures of build 202610101724 against `~/.ripul/theme-reference/baseline`, on the baseline's own simulator (iPhone 18 Pro, iOS 27.0). 50 are identical or within noise of 3. The rest:

| Screen | Difference | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `session-list` light, dark | x 1061-1104, y 1238-1466 | The animated machine glyph on the two running rows. Two captures of this build differ in the same box. |
| `session-rows-busy` (3) | spinners | By-eye screen. |
| `start-chooser` (4) | the wordmark's dot | By-eye screen. |
| `title-lozenge-list-light` | x 573-625, y 1377-1429 | The "Connecting" spinner. Same box between two captures of this build. |
| `explorer-dark` | 2 pixels, difference of 4 | Gone on the second capture. |
| `title-lozenge-light` | 4.3% | My first capture was a blank white screen: the app had not drawn. The second is identical to the baseline. |

- **Capture script:** it failed three times at its first launch after its own simulator restart ("Launchd job spawn failed"). I ran it through a wrapper in `/tmp` that retries a launch; the script itself is unchanged.
- **Status bar:** the strip is not compared, and the baseline shows a Dynamic Island there that my captures do not.

## 3. The loud switch

Fixtures ran by launch argument in light and dark (I looked at five of the 14 light captures: the two session-list screens, standalone, start chooser, macro capture). On the Duo I looked at about 20 signed-in screens, first after a live switch and then after a cold start.

- **Wrong role:** none that I could see.
- **Resized symbol:** none seen. A static scan of the 606 in-scope files also finds no text-role font on a container holding only symbols (a heuristic, so reasoned).
- **Fixed:** nothing. Each item below is a judgement or is system-drawn.

What did not change:

- **Empty states.** `ContentUnavailableView` keeps the system font and greys. Seen at `NoPairedMacView.swift:46`; there are 39 uses in 21 in-scope files.
- **Grouped lists.** List and Form grounds and row grounds stay the system's (Settings, Trainyard, Artefacts, To Do, Devices, the Models sheet, Paired Macs), while custom screens take canvas. Section headers take the family but stay system grey.
- **Start chooser.** Its ground stays white (`RuntimeModeRoot.swift`).
- **Dividers.** `Divider()` is the system's, not `separator` (111 in scope, including `RuntimeModeRoot.swift:99`).
- **Destructive buttons.** `Button(role: .destructive)` stays system red, not `danger`: Repair Connection, Clear Session Data, Archive All Chats, Factory Reset (`SettingsScreen.swift:691`). 127 uses in scope.
- **Text-level `.monospaced()`.** It stays the system monospaced face, not the code family: `TrainyardScreen.swift:707`, `TrainyardConfig.swift:199`, `MacHostBuilds.swift:499`, `PlanReviewDetailView.swift:401`, `PlanCreateSheet.swift:61`. Seen on screen for the first; the others are from a grep.
- **Text with no colour of its own.** Session titles, commit subjects and most row titles stay black. In Settings, "Claude accounts" and "Codex accounts" (`SettingsScreen.swift:463`) take the text role while their neighbours do not.
- **System-drawn, as the foundation predicted, now seen.** The More list, unselected tab icons, the large navigation title on Paired Macs, inline sheet titles, segmented labels, menu-picker values, and a prominent button's label (white, not `onAccent`).
- **No live repaint.** The composer's placeholder took the loud face only after a relaunch, and kept it after switching back until the next relaunch.

## 4. The signed-in walk (iPhone Duo, iOS 27.1, unfolded; looked only)

- **Default document:** sessions list with a chat, the More list, Devices, Repos and a repo's History, Memories, Archived (still loading), Settings, Trainyard. Nothing looked wrong.
- **Loud document:** sessions list and chat, sidebar, Trainyard, Settings (top and bottom), browser chrome, Files, Artefacts, Paired Macs, Repos and History, Processes (still loading), Console, Dock, To Do, Solutions, the Models sheet, Devices, the New Chat sheet.
- **Not reached:**
  - Plans, Voice Mode, Live View and the remote window
  - Memories and Archived with content, Remote Tabs, CMS Test Bed, Settings sub-pages
  - the model picker, composer menus, the native tool strip and tool detail sheets
  - onboarding, pricing, What's New
  - any alert, menu or swipe action
  - dark mode on the signed-in app, and all of Mac Catalyst
- **Left as found:** the Duo is back on the default document, relaunched, and a closing capture matches the one from the start. The device and both simulator leases are released.
- **Simulator screenshots:** `simctl io screenshot` went black on the Duo part-way through while the app kept running, so later captures are the device tool's.

## 5. Web, tests, WAC

- **Web snapshot (ran, live build `mv2ky8ec`, under a hold):** identical, 17,012 elements over 18 page-modes. The live build holds every web commit on `main`.
- **Chat in the app (looked, not measured):** it followed the loud document live and returned with the default one. Message text stayed sans-serif under loud. I had no tool to read computed styles on the device.
- **Web theme tests (ran):** 16 of 16. Both literal checks read zero.
- **SDK theme tests:** 66 on macOS and 73 on the iOS simulator, with the same one failure in both: `RemoteThemeClientTests.testNotModifiedRestoresServerOverLocalPreview` (`RemoteThemeClientTests.swift:79`). Neither the test nor `RemoteThemeClient.swift` was touched by this plan (last changed 6 October), so I take it as older; that is reasoned from history, not run on an earlier commit.
- **WAC's real theme file:** the test that loads it is iOS-only. It ran on the simulator and passed, not skipped.
- **WAC compile (ran, by a sub-agent):** `v3` at e21efc8b1 in a `/tmp` worktree pointed at the local SDK built for the arm64 simulator with no WAC source changed. The worktree is removed.
- **WAC with arm64 and x86_64 together:** it fails inside the SDK at `MainThreadSampler.swift:141`. The same line is in 0.7.169, so it is not from this plan.
- **WAC pin bump:** the local SDK now needs `thinking-orbs-swift` 0.2.0.

## 6. What a brand theme would visibly get wrong today

1. Half the app would not take a brand canvas or surface. Every grouped list keeps the system's grey and white, so Settings, Trainyard, Artefacts, To Do and Devices would sit in different grounds from Files, Repos, Dock and the sessions list. The start chooser stays white.
2. Two typefaces on one screen: navigation titles, segmented controls, picker values, the More list and every empty state stay in the system font, and chat message text stays sans-serif.
3. If the theme sets a text colour, titles stay black beside coloured detail text.
4. Destructive buttons stay system red whatever `danger` is, next to accent-tinted icons.
5. Dividers stay system grey whatever `separator` is.
6. A live switch leaves the composer in the old face until relaunch.
7. Commit hashes in Trainyard (seen), and by the code also Mac builds and Plans, stay in the system monospaced face.

Captures, comparisons and logs are in `/tmp/theme-verify`.

input.task:
You are building the first thing a person can actually see from the plan at docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.md in this repository: a trial brand theme. Today every font and colour in Ripul's apps and web chat comes from theme accessors, and a document chosen by a link switches the whole look in a Debug build. Only two documents exist: the default (the system look) and a deliberately garish test one. Peter, whose product this is, started all of this because the app does not look like the website (app.ripul.io). He has not yet seen anything change. Your job is a third document that carries the website's brand, so he can switch to it and look.

This is a trial to look at, not the finished brand step. Keep it small and get it in front of him.

READ FIRST
- The plan: Decision 1 ("Where exactly stops"), Decision 5 (what was measured on iPhone and on Mac Catalyst), and "The brand theme", including "What verification found".
- `ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md`, whole: the document's shape, families, type roles, "The loud document" (how a bundled document is chosen), "Limits".
- `chrome-extension/docs/features/ui/themingGuide.md`: the first-party theme, the families, "The document from the native shell".
- `website/public/css/site.css` (the `:root` block): the brand's values. `website/public/fonts/` has Archivo and Instrument Serif as woff2.
- ripul_guide topics `plans`, `trains`, `devices`, and `voice-and-media` (for showing pictures).
- Your plan task is t_0f3ecf875f7c: mark it doing now with planTaskStatus, write to its note as you go, and mark it done at the end with your report. The host drops agent messages when it reloads; the plan's log is the record.

WHAT TO BUILD
1. `theme/ripul-theme-brand.json`, chosen exactly as the loud document is (`ripul://theme?name=ripul-theme-brand`, and the launch argument). The default document does not change, and nobody who does not open that link sees anything different.
   - Accent: the website's teal, `#1f6f70` in light and `#62b9b4` in dark.
   - Text family: Archivo. Display family: Instrument Serif. Code family: unchanged.
   - Canvas, surfaces and text colours: NOT set. Peter decided the brand keeps the neutral system canvas first.
   - `onAccent`: check white against each accent for contrast and choose what passes; say what you measured.
   - The section-header role may take the website's letter-spacing if the document can express it.
2. The fonts, bundled so the app can draw them: Archivo and Instrument Serif (regular and italic). The website has only woff2; the app needs the original font files. Both families are under the SIL Open Font License and are in Google's public fonts repository on GitHub; take them from there, keep the licence files beside them, and say exactly where each file came from. Check two things the plan asks about before relying on Archivo: that weights work (semibold and bold must draw as such; if the variable font does not take SwiftUI's weight, bundle static weights), and that it has fixed-width digits for the session rows' timers.
3. The web chat follows through the handoff that already exists. Make the two families available to the web as web fonts and make sure a document naming them resolves; under the default document the web is unchanged (the snapshot must stay identical).
4. The serif on one or two display moments only, if the display role is already read there; do not go hunting. Never on navigation titles, rows or buttons.

WHAT YOU MAY CHANGE
The new document, the font files and their registration, and what the trial genuinely needs in `ThemeCore/`, the app's theme loading and the web's font families. The streams are finished, so file ownership is no longer the constraint; the constraint is that the default document's behaviour does not move: the theme tests (which assert each default equals the system value), both checks and the web snapshot must still pass, and you run them. Do not try to fix what "What verification found" lists (grouped lists, system-drawn titles, empty states, dividers, destructive buttons, the composer's repaint): those are the next step. Do not make the brand the default.

SHOW IT
On a borrowed simulator, with the simulator train: the session list fixture, the sidebar, a chat, Settings, and one sheet, each under the default document and under the brand one, in light and in dark. Save the pictures under /tmp/theme-brand/ with plain names (for example `session-list-light-default.png`, `session-list-light-brand.png`), and write `/tmp/theme-brand/INDEX.md` listing each pair in one line. I will show them to Peter. Look at every picture yourself before you report: say what is good and, plainly, what looks wrong (two typefaces on one screen, a title left in the system font, text that is too wide or clipped, a weight that did not take, symbols that moved).
If you use the signed-in iPhone Duo simulator for the screens that need an account (Peter allows agents to take it over): look only, send nothing, change no settings, and when you finish switch it back to the default document, confirm that with a capture, and release it.

RULES
- Do not install to Peter's iPhone. I will ask him.
- Many sessions share this checkout. Commit only your own files: `git add <paths>`, then `git commit -m "…" -- <paths>`; never a bare `git commit`; if git says the index is locked, wait and retry; push at once; never stash, reset or check out files.
- Compile before every push (theming.md gives the commands; the SDK build for the iOS simulator uses `--triple`). `npx tsgo --noEmit` after any web change, and deploy the web only through `npm run deploy:all`.
- Say for every claim whether you ran it, looked at it, or reasoned it.

YOUR REPORT, IN THE TASK NOTE AND AS YOUR FINAL REPLY
The commits and what was deployed; where each font file came from and what you checked about weights and digits; the contrast you measured for `onAccent`; that the tests, both checks and the web snapshot still pass under the default document; the list of picture pairs; and your own honest read of how the brand looks: what works, and the three or four things Peter will notice are wrong.

content.text:
Verification is finished, and I've started the one piece you can actually look at: a trial brand theme.

## Verification verdict

"Nothing changed" holds everywhere it could be measured, but that is a small part of the app.

- **Measured and clean:** 50 of 56 reference captures are identical or within noise. The other six are animated spots, or one capture taken before the app had drawn; its retake matched. The web snapshot is identical across about 17,000 elements. WAC compiles.
- **Looked at, no baseline:** nine signed-in screens under the normal theme looked normal. About twenty changed fully under the garish test theme, with no stray literal or wrong role seen.
- **Not reached at all:** Plans, Voice Mode, Live View, Settings sub-pages, any alert, menu or swipe action, dark mode on the signed-in app, and all of Mac Catalyst.
- **Your simulator:** the iPhone Duo is back on the normal theme, confirmed by a closing capture.

The agent changed no code: nothing it found was a mechanical fix.

## What a brand theme would still get wrong

These are parts the system draws, which no accessor reaches:

1. **Grouped lists** (Settings, Trainyard, Artefacts, To Do, Devices) keep the system's backgrounds. This only matters if the canvas changes, and you chose neutral.
2. **Two typefaces on one screen.** Navigation titles, segmented controls, picker values and every empty state stay in the system font, and chat message text stays sans-serif.
3. **Destructive buttons** stay system red, and **dividers** stay system grey.
4. **The composer** takes a new typeface only after a relaunch.

Item 2 is the one you will notice with Archivo.

## What's running

One agent ("Theme: brand trial") is building a third theme: teal accent, Archivo for text, Instrument Serif for display, neutral canvas. It is switched on by a link in Debug builds, and the default is untouched. It will capture the session list, sidebar, a chat, Settings and a sheet, before and after, in light and dark. I'll show you those pictures, then ask about putting it on your phone.

Dark mode: prominent buttons (Continue, Pair a Mac, Normal) keep a white label on the light teal, the 2.3:1 pair; the system draws that label and onAccent does not reach it. 3. Settings: section headers lose their semibold and the footer grows to body size, because the root's default font replaces the form's own header and footer styles. 4. Two typefaces on a screen: toolbar titles (Agents, Settings, the chat title), the Help sheet's title, empty states (No Paired Mac) and the composer's placeholder stay in the system font. 5. Machine icons and the help mark stay system blue beside the teal. 8. Archivo sets tighter: rows and lists are a few points shorter, so everything shifts up. 9. After switching back to the default by link, the chat's two tool rows drew smaller until a relaunch.

NOT DONE: eyebrow tracking is in the document but nothing reads ripulTextStyle(.eyebrow); Mac Catalyst not looked at; plan log files left uncommitted (they hold other sessions' lines too).

Each line is one screen under the default document and under `theme/ripul-theme-brand.json`, in light and in dark.
`sheets/` holds the same pictures side by side (default left, brand right), which is the quickest way to look.

## Signed-out simulator (iPhone 18 Pro Max, iOS 27.0), fixtures, full-size PNG

- Session list fixture: `session-list-{light,dark}-default.png` / `session-list-{light,dark}-brand.png` (sheet: `sheets/session-list.png`)
- Session rows fixture: `session-rows-{light,dark}-default.png` / `session-rows-{light,dark}-brand.png` (sheet: `sheets/session-rows.png`)
- What's New (the serif title): `whats-new-{light,dark}-default.png` / `whats-new-{light,dark}-brand.png` (sheet: `sheets/whats-new.png`)
- Start chooser: `start-chooser-{light,dark}-default.png` / `start-chooser-{light,dark}-brand.png` (sheet: `sheets/start-chooser.png`)
- Standalone workspace, no Mac paired (an empty state): `standalone-chat-{light,dark}-default.png` / `standalone-chat-{light,dark}-brand.png` (sheet: `sheets/standalone-chat.png`)

## Signed-in iPhone Duo simulator (iOS 27.1), 951 px JPEG from the app's own frame tool

- Session list beside a chat: `list-and-chat-{light,dark}-default.jpg` / `list-and-chat-{light,dark}-brand.jpg` (sheets: `sheets/list-and-chat-light.png`, `-dark.png`)
- Sidebar: `sidebar-{light,dark}-default.jpg` / `sidebar-{light,dark}-brand.jpg` (sheets: `sheets/sidebar-light.png`, `-dark.png`)
- Settings: `settings-{light,dark}-default.jpg` / `settings-{light,dark}-brand.jpg` (sheets: `sheets/settings-light.png`, `-dark.png`)
- A sheet, Help (its body is the website, so it is also the look to aim at): `sheet-help-{light,dark}-default.jpg` / `sheet-help-{light,dark}-brand.jpg` (sheets: `sheets/sheet-help-light.png`, `-dark.png`)

## Other

- `duo-after-switching-back-default.jpg`: the Duo straight after switching back to the default document, before a relaunch. The two tool rows in the chat are smaller than they were.
- `duo-restored-default-confirmation.jpg`: the Duo after a relaunch, on the default document, as it was found.
- `work/`: logs, the capture script, the font probe and its `weights.png`.

Not captured: the onboarding screen without the notification alert over it (its title is the same serif as What's New), and anything on Mac Catalyst.

content.text:
Yes, finished. Nothing is running. The brand trial marked itself done at 18:23; its reply never reached this chat, so I read its report from the plan log.

The four pictures above are today on the left and the trial brand theme on the right (the last one has light and dark). I looked at each.

**What works**
- **Session list and sidebar:** Archivo throughout, teal tags and icons. They read as one product with the wordmark.
- **Settings:** icons go teal and rows take Archivo.
- **The fonts hold up:** Archivo takes every weight from one file and has fixed-width digits for the timers.

**What is wrong**
1. **The chat does not change at all.** Message text keeps the same face under both themes, so the list is Archivo and the chat beside it is not.
2. **The serif title is thin and small.** "Trainyard" on What's New is 28-point regular where a bold sans was. It needs its own size.
3. **Dark mode buttons fail contrast.** "Continue" is a white label on light teal, about 2.3 to 1. The system draws that label, so the theme cannot reach it.
4. **Settings regresses.** Section headers lose their semibold and the footer text grows to body size.
5. **Toolbar titles, empty states and the composer's placeholder stay in the system font.**
6. **Machine icons and the help mark stay system blue** beside the teal.

The agent also reports that onboarding descriptions truncate to one line under the brand, and that Archivo sets tighter, so rows shift up a few points. I have not checked those two myself.

Nothing changed for anyone by default: the trial is switched on by a link in Debug builds only. Your iPhone Duo simulator is back on the normal theme.

**Next step.** I'd fix 1, 3 and 4 before you judge it, since they are defects and not taste. Or I can put this build on your phone now so you can flip between the two yourself. Which do you want?

description: "When a feature can only be tried after an SDK release, a WAC change and builds, Peter expects the whole chain done, not a stop to ask"
metadata:

3 October 2026, support sessions: I finished the Ripul side, then stopped and asked Peter three things (publish the SDK to the public repo? where does Get Help go in WAC? which phones?). His reply was "Why can't you do all that". I then published SDK 0.7.165, changed WAC, and published both builds over the air without further questions.

**Why:** (my reading) he had already said to use WAC as the test app, which implies the release, the pin bump and the builds; asking again cost him a round trip for work he considered part of the task. The repo's own rules already allow commits, pushes and WAC shipping without asking.

**How to apply:** when he names the app to test in, carry the feature all the way to an installable build of that app: SDK release (`release-public.sh` from a clean worktree), WAC pin and change, OTA or device install. Pick the placement myself, keep anything unfinished out of the App Store build (WAC: `#if WAC_DEVELOPER_TOOLS`), and report what was done and what could not be verified. Still ask first for destructive git, force pushes, and sending touches to a phone somebody may be holding (see the device runner memory). Scope: this is one remark on one feature, not a blanket instruction.

Related: [[feedback_deploy_flow]], [[feedback_permission_friction]], [[project_wac_payslip_repo]].

---
name: feedback-finish-the-release-chain
description: "For Peter, done means on his phone and visible. Do not stop at committed or simulator-verified and ask about the last step; he has said this twice (3 and 10 Oct 2026)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 011c0769-ffa1-4a7b-affd-e820e2399e72
  modified: 2026-10-10T18:10:00.000Z
---

Peter has now made the same complaint twice, so treat it as a standing rule, not a one-off.

**3 October 2026, support sessions:** I finished the Ripul side, then stopped and asked Peter three things (publish the SDK to the public repo? where does Get Help go in WAC? which phones?). His reply was "Why can't you do all that". I then published SDK 0.7.165, changed WAC, and published both builds over the air without further questions.

**10 October 2026, theme migration (chat "Design alignment"):** after a day in which about fifteen agents moved the app onto theme tokens and one built a trial brand theme, everything was committed and shown on simulators, and I ended my turn with "fix these first, or put it on your phone: which do you want?". His words: "it's all finished, but nothing's actually deployed, nothing's running, nothing's on my phone. Basically, nothing, nothing, nothing", then "this just seems like a familiar story. Nothing ever does get actually done. Why do you always stop before the final step?" I then shipped the build to his phone through the iOS train without asking.

**Why:** (my reading) he judges progress by what is on his phone and what he can see, not by commits, checks or simulator pictures. A turn that ends on a question about the last step reads to him as nothing done, and costs him a round trip for work the repo's rules already allow (commit, push, train builds, installs to his own phone).

**How to apply:**
- When work reaches "committed and verified by me", keep going: ship it to his iPhone through the train (`ship_ios.py`, see [[feedback_deploy_flow]]) in the same turn, confirm the build landed, and only then report. Say plainly what is on the phone and what he will see.
- If the change is behind a switch (a theme link, a flag), flip the switch for him and say how to flip it back; do not leave the last tap as homework.
- Do not end a turn with "which do you want?" when one of the options is simply the next step and is already authorised. Do it, then offer the alternative.
- On long multi-agent work, get something visible onto his phone early, not after the plumbing is complete: a whole day with nothing to look at is what made him call it "nothing".
- Still ask first for destructive git, force pushes, TestFlight or App Store uploads (see [[feedback_no_testflight]]), and sending touches to a phone somebody may be holding. An install restarts the app, so if he is in a voice conversation on that phone, tell him it is about to restart; that is a warning, not a question.

Related: [[feedback_deploy_flow]], [[feedback_permission_friction]], [[project_wac_payslip_repo]], [[feedback_ask_me_to_test]].

input.title: Theme: brand fixes, native
input.task:
You are fixing the defects in Ripul's trial brand theme on the native side, and then putting the result on the owner's iPhone. Read this whole brief before starting.

WHERE THINGS STAND
Peter, whose product this is, has the trial brand theme running on his iPhone right now (build 202610101906, switched to `theme/ripul-theme-brand.json`: the website's teal accent, Archivo for text, Instrument Serif for display, neutral canvas). His words a few minutes ago: "This is looking way more integrated. I love how it feels", and he gave full permission to go ahead and make the remaining changes. So this is no longer a trial to look at: fix what is wrong with it. He judges progress by what is on his phone, and has said twice that work which stops at "committed" reads to him as nothing done. Your job ends when the fixes are on his phone.

READ FIRST
- docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.md: Decision 1 ("Where exactly stops"), Decision 5 (what was measured on iPhone and Mac Catalyst), "The brand theme" with "What verification found".
- ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md, whole.
- In docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.review.md, the task note of the brand trial (search for "Trial brand theme built and pictured"): its nine "what looks wrong" items are your list. Its pictures are in /tmp/theme-brand/ (INDEX.md and sheets/).
- .ripul/memories/project_theme_migration_s1_lessons.md.
- ripul_guide topics `plans`, `trains`, `devices`.
- Your plan task is t_c156a58b9c4d: mark it doing now with planTaskStatus, write to its note as you go, and mark it done at the end with your report. Agent messages get lost when the host reloads; the plan's log is the record.

WHAT TO FIX, IN THIS ORDER
1. Prominent buttons in dark mode. The dark accent is the light teal `#62b9b4`; white on it is 2.3 to 1. The document already sets `onAccent` to the website's ink for dark (6.5 to 1), but the system draws a prominent button's label white and never reads it (Continue, Pair a Mac, Normal). Make prominent buttons draw their label in `onAccent` under a theme.
2. Forms under a themed family. In Settings the section headers lose their semibold and the footers grow to body size, because the root's default font replaces the form's own header and footer styles. The plan's reviewer predicted this: an absent environment font is how controls choose their own. Find a way for text with no font of its own to take the family without overriding what a control chooses for itself, or style headers and footers explicitly. Check the other grouped screens too (Trainyard, Devices, To Do, Artefacts).
3. Text the system draws, which stays in the system font beside Archivo: navigation and toolbar titles (large and inline), sheet titles, segmented controls, tab bar labels, picker values, and every empty state (`ContentUnavailableView`, 39 uses; "No Paired Mac" is one and is in the reference fixtures). Use UIKit's appearance settings where the system draws the text, set from the theme, refreshed when the theme changes and put back to the system's when the default document returns. For empty states, give them labels that read the accessors.
4. The composer's placeholder takes a new face only after a relaunch, and keeps it after switching back. Make it follow a switch.
5. The serif. On What's New and onboarding the title is 28 point regular where a bold sans was, and reads thin and small; Instrument Serif has one weight. Give the display role a size of its own in the brand document so it carries, and fix the onboarding descriptions that truncate to one line under the brand.
6. Icons left system blue beside the teal: the machine icons in the session list and sidebar, and the help mark. Find what each is today by the closed table. Where the blue meant "the app's colour", it should follow the accent under the brand; where it is data or status, leave it. The stream that migrated the sidebar flagged two more it thought meant the accent: the chat-bubble blue in ScreenSwitcherOverlay.swift near line 1031 and the person icon in SessionInviteView.
7. If there is time after 1 to 6: on Mac Catalyst the window's tint does not cross a presentation, so a presented hosting controller that is not a theme root gets no accent, and neither does a popover's content. Ten of the SDK's hosting controllers are not roots. Make them and the popovers roots. Peter uses the Catalyst app daily.

THE ONE RULE THAT MUST NOT BREAK
With the default document nothing may change. Everyone who has not switched themes, and the one other app built on the SDK, sees the default. So after your changes: the SDK theme tests pass (they assert each default equals the system value), `check_theme_tokens.py` reads zero, the rewrite script's lint passes on your diff, the SDK builds for the iOS simulator (the `--triple` form) and for macOS, the app compiles, and the reference screens under the default document still match the baseline at ~/.ripul/theme-reference/baseline (theming.md, "Checking your work", step 6; the S1 memory says how captures go wrong). An appearance setting applied under the default document is the likeliest way to break this: apply nothing when no theme names a value.

HOW TO WORK
- Fix one item, look at it under the brand document in light and dark on a borrowed simulator, then the next. Save before-and-after pictures under /tmp/theme-brand-fixes/ with plain names and an INDEX.md, as the trial did.
- Many sessions share this checkout. Commit only your own files: `git add <paths>`, then `git commit -m "…" -- <paths>`; never a bare `git commit`; if git says the index is locked, wait and retry; push at once; never stash, reset or check out files. A compile error in a file that is not yours is another session mid-edit: wait and build again.
- A second agent is fixing the web chat at the same time (the chat's message text does not take the family). It owns everything under chrome-extension/. You own the native side.

THE LAST STEP, WHICH IS YOURS
When items 1 to 6 are fixed, committed, pushed and checked as above, put the build on Peter's iPhone: from the repository root, `RIPUL_DEVICE_ID=00008150-001C544E0EBA401C python3 ripul-native-app/scripts/ship_ios.py --variants main`, run detached with nohup and a log, as CLAUDE.md describes for long jobs. It boards the iOS train, installs and relaunches the app; that is expected, he knows. His phone stays on the brand document across the install. Confirm from the log that it installed and was verified, and put the build number in your report. Do not wait to be asked and do not stop at "committed". If one item proves hard, ship the others and say which is left.
Do not change the default document, do not make the brand the default, and do not touch TestFlight.

YOUR REPORT, IN THE TASK NOTE AND AS YOUR FINAL REPLY
For each item: fixed or not, how, and whether you looked at it on a simulator. The checks you ran under the default document and their results. The build number on Peter's phone. What still looks wrong, plainly.

input.title: Theme: brand fixes, web chat
input.task:
You are fixing the web chat's part of Ripul's trial brand theme. Read this whole brief before starting.

WHERE THINGS STAND
Ripul's native app now takes its fonts and colours from a theme document, and the chat (a web view inside the app) receives the document the app adopted, at start and on each change. Peter, whose product this is, has the trial brand theme running on his iPhone right now (`theme/ripul-theme-brand.json`: the website's teal accent, Archivo for text, Instrument Serif for display). His words a few minutes ago: "This is looking way more integrated. I love how it feels", and he gave full permission to go ahead and make the remaining changes. The most visible defect left is yours: the native screens around the chat are in Archivo and teal, and the chat itself has not changed. The web is served live, so your fix reaches his phone as soon as it is deployed; no app build is needed.

READ FIRST
- `chrome-extension/docs/features/ui/themingGuide.md`, whole: the first-party theme, the families, the named colours, "The document from the native shell", the snapshot and the literals check.
- docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.md: Decision 6 and "The brand theme".
- In docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.review.md, three task notes: the handoff (search "B1 done"), the brand trial (search "Trial brand theme built and pictured"), and the verification pass. Between them they say what the chat does and does not take from a document today.
- `.ripul/memories/reference_first_party_chat_in_clean_webkit.md`.
- ripul_guide topics `plans`, `trains`, `devices` and `browser`.
- Your plan task is t_97a9aaca35dd: mark it doing now with planTaskStatus, write to its note as you go, and mark it done at the end with your report. Agent messages get lost when the host reloads; the plan's log is the record.

WHAT TO FIX, IN THIS ORDER
1. Message text does not take the theme's text family. Under the brand document the chat's messages draw in the same face as under the default. The web foundation found why the default looks as it does: the page body is `sans-serif` and only MUI's own components draw in the theme's family, so message text inherits the body. It left open whether the text family should reach the page body. That is now decided: under a document that names a text family, it reaches the body and everything that inherits from it (assistant text, user messages, tool rows, the composer if the web draws it). Under the default document nothing changes.
2. A themed accent does not reach everything. The first-party base themes hard-code the old blue inside their component overrides (`lightTheme.ts` has `#0078d4` and its rgba in MuiCheckbox, MuiOutlinedInput and others), and when a document sets the accent only the main palette value changes: the derived shades (`primary.light`, `primary.dark`) keep the old colour, and the user bubble reads `primary.light`. Under a document that sets the accent, the overrides must read the palette and the shades must be derived from it.
3. The other teals and the empty chat's accents. The chat has its own teals that are not the accent (the user message accent `#00897B` and `#4DB6AC`, a tool-call teal, the empty chat's four dot colours), now held as named colours. Under the brand document they should agree with the accent: say how a document reaches a named colour, do it if the document's shape allows it cleanly, and if it does not, say what would have to change and leave it.
4. Going back. The brand trial saw that after switching back to the default document by link, the chat's two tool rows drew smaller until the app was relaunched. Find it and fix it: a switch back must restore the default exactly, with no relaunch.
5. The display family. If the empty chat's serif heading still declares its own font face and does not read the theme's display family, make it read it.

THE ONE RULE THAT MUST NOT BREAK
With the default document, and for every site-key customer, nothing may change. After your changes the computed-style snapshot against the committed baseline is identical (it was 17,012 elements over 18 page-modes), the literals check reads zero for the first-party scope, `npx tsgo --noEmit` is clean, and the theme tests pass. Everything you add applies only under the first-party presentation and only when the document names the value.

HOW TO PROVE IT
- The snapshot, as above, for the default.
- For the brand: in the app on a borrowed simulator (the simulator train puts the current build on it; the app adopts a bundled document by `ripul://theme?name=ripul-theme-brand`), with a chat on screen, switch to the brand document and read the computed font family and colours of message text, a user message, a tool row and a checkbox or input from the chat's web view, before and after, and then after switching back. Save before-and-after pictures under /tmp/theme-brand-web/ with plain names and an INDEX.md, and look at them yourself.
- Deploy through `npm run deploy:all` from a committed and pushed tree, and confirm what went live (`verify:pages`). The worker step has failed today on a Cloudflare authorisation error unrelated to this work; if it does, check that Pages shipped and say so.

RULES
- Many sessions share this checkout, and a second agent is fixing the native side at the same time: it owns everything outside chrome-extension/, you own chrome-extension/. toolu_01Ciz8jg6CLrH6mytsxmRwao.task:
You are fixing the web chat's part of Ripul's trial brand theme. Read this whole brief before starting.

WHERE THINGS STAND
Ripul's native app now takes its fonts and colours from a theme document, and the chat (a web view inside the app) receives the document the app adopted, at start and on each change. Peter, whose product this is, has the trial brand theme running on his iPhone right now (`theme/ripul-theme-brand.json`: the website's teal accent, Archivo for text, Instrument Serif for display). His words a few minutes ago: "This is looking way more integrated. I love how it feels", and he gave full permission to go ahead and make the remaining changes. The most visible defect left is yours: the native screens around the chat are in Archivo and teal, and the chat itself has not changed. The web is served live, so your fix reaches his phone as soon as it is deployed; no app build is needed.

READ FIRST
- `chrome-extension/docs/features/ui/themingGuide.md`, whole: the first-party theme, the families, the named colours, "The document from the native shell", the snapshot and the literals check.
- docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.md: Decision 6 and "The brand theme".
- In docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.review.md, three task notes: the handoff (search "B1 done"), the brand trial (search "Trial brand theme built and pictured"), and the verification pass. Between them they say what the chat does and does not take from a document today.
- `.ripul/memories/reference_first_party_chat_in_clean_webkit.md`.
- ripul_guide topics `plans`, `trains`, `devices` and `browser`.
- Your plan task is t_97a9aaca35dd: mark it doing now with planTaskStatus, write to its note as you go, and mark it done at the end with your report. Agent messages get lost when the host reloads; the plan's log is the record.

WHAT TO FIX, IN THIS ORDER
1. Message text does not take the theme's text family. Under the brand document the chat's messages draw in the same face as under the default. The web foundation found why the default looks as it does: the page body is `sans-serif` and only MUI's own components draw in the theme's family, so message text inherits the body. It left open whether the text family should reach the page body. That is now decided: under a document that names a text family, it reaches the body and everything that inherits from it (assistant text, user messages, tool rows, the composer if the web draws it). Under the default document nothing changes.
2. A themed accent does not reach everything. The first-party base themes hard-code the old blue inside their component overrides (`lightTheme.ts` has `#0078d4` and its rgba in MuiCheckbox, MuiOutlinedInput and others), and when a document sets the accent only the main palette value changes: the derived shades (`primary.light`, `primary.dark`) keep the old colour, and the user bubble reads `primary.light`. Under a document that sets the accent, the overrides must read the palette and the shades must be derived from it.
3. The other teals and the empty chat's accents. The chat has its own teals that are not the accent (the user message accent `#00897B` and `#4DB6AC`, a tool-call teal, the empty chat's four dot colours), now held as named colours. Under the brand document they should agree with the accent: say how a document reaches a named colour, do it if the document's shape allows it cleanly, and if it does not, say what would have to change and leave it.
4. Going back. The brand trial saw that after switching back to the default document by link, the chat's two tool rows drew smaller until the app was relaunched. Find it and fix it: a switch back must restore the default exactly, with no relaunch.
5. The display family. If the empty chat's serif heading still declares its own font face and does not read the theme's display family, make it read it.

COMMITS (main, pushed): 06e6de8df accent carries its shades, the base theme's literals and the chat's accents; text family reaches the page root and the tool rows. efb09d463 plain buttons inherit the family; guide. c39e0cac4 the root rule as `html body` (found on the simulator: right after a live switch, lost at page start). 56e6e19e3 native slots measure again on a document change. 23321ad67 guide. Docs: themingGuide.md "What an accent carries", "The text family and the page root".
DEPLOYED: deploy:all twice. train_900 (efb09d463): pages verified mv2q83t5, worker step failed on Cloudflare 7403. train_903 (56e6e19e3): pages verified mv2qdxzc, worker step exited 0. Nothing installed on Peter's iPhone.

1. TEXT FAMILY, fixed. Under the first-party presentation, when the document names a text family, AppThemeProvider writes `html body { font-family }` and `button { font-family: inherit }`. Simulator (iPhone Duo, real chat, light), default / brand / back: body sans-serif / Archivo, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif / sans-serif. Tally of data-ui elements by first family: default sans-serif 347, Roboto 20, system-ui 36, -apple-system 12, monospace 4; brand Archivo 400, system-ui 3, -apple-system 12, monospace 4; back equal to default. Assistant paragraph, user message, tool header, timestamp, model label all compute Archivo under brand. Before the fix (mv2ne5af) brand gave Archivo 20, sans-serif 347.
2. ACCENT, fixed. When the document sets the accent: primary.light = lighten 0.2, primary.dark = darken 0.3 (light mode: rgb(75,139,140) and rgb(21,77,78) from #1f6f70); every literal of the base theme's old main, light and dark, as hex and as rgba, is replaced in components, toolbar, settings, sidebar, dialog and the palette. The theme files are not edited, so no other theme object changes. A base whose accent has no hue (darkMinimal, white) has no literal replaced. Read in a clean WebKit on the live build: focused input outline and label rgb(0,120,212) / rgb(31,111,112) / rgb(0,120,212); send button colour and its 0.15 and 0.3 washes the same way; the one primary.light element rgb(79,163,231) / rgb(75,139,140); dark mode accent rgb(98,185,180). No checkbox is on a reference page; the checkbox hover override is asserted in the unit test (rgba(31,111,112,0.04)).
3. OTHER TEALS, fixed through the accent. A document reaches a named colour only through its accent role: panels.userMessageAccent, starter.accent, the four starter.dots and palette.tool become the accent. Read: user message tint rgba(0,137,123,0.06) / rgba(31,111,112,0.06) light, rgba(77,182,172,0.08) / rgba(98,185,180,0.08) dark; empty chat dots, four colours under default, one under brand. Not possible without a grammar change: a document setting one named colour by itself. That needs a place in the document (a role per named colour or a web-only section) and the native reader taught to pass it by. secondary.main (#40e0d0, the third teal the plan names) is left alone: it is not in the brief's list and is another hue in two base themes.
4. GOING BACK, fixed; it was two faults. (a) The tool rows' family was read once at page start; FeatureScopeProvider now sets it from the theme on each render. (b) The fault the trial saw, reproduced on build mv2q83t5: app started under brand, switched back by link, the two agent rows' native slots stay 55.7 high where the default is 58.3. The native side measures a row once and the web slot kept that height. NativeEmbedSlot now forgets the height and starts a new native lifetime on a document change. On mv2qdxzc: default 58.3, brand 55.7, back 58.3; started under brand then back: every value and all 56 row sizes equal to the default reading, no relaunch.
5. DISPLAY FAMILY, already right, nothing changed: the empty chat's title reads fontFamiliesOf(theme).display. Read: Instrument Serif under default and brand.

DEFAULT DOCUMENT UNCHANGED. Snapshot of 06e6de8df built in a /tmp worktree against the committed baseline: identical, 17,012 elements. Snapshot of the live final build mv2qdxzc: 17 of 18 page-modes identical in the full run; control-fixture-not-first-party@dark showed 103 differences, all one row of tools folded to a count (1360 elements against 1459); captured again alone it is 1459 elements and identical. Literals check: first-party scope hex 0, rgba 0, fontFamily 0. tsgo clean. Theme tests 22 pass (5 new), chatPresentation tests 5 pass. On the simulator the default reading on mv2qdxzc equals the reading on mv2ne5af.
NOT RUN: Mac Catalyst; dark mode in the app (dark read in WebKit only); the six dark base themes other than darkGradient in a browser (darkMinimal unit-tested); a native interaction form open during a document change (its slot is remounted too).

WHAT THE CHAT STILL DOES NOT TAKE FROM A DOCUMENT: the code block's frame and language label (-apple-system stack in markdownThemeStyles.ts, marked deferred); code and paths unless the document names a code family; the native-look tool strip labels (they copy the system's); the markdown sheet's own

# Brand theme fixes: before and after

Signed-out simulator (iPhone 18 Pro Max, iOS 27.0), commit `c4abaf274`.
`-before` is the trial's picture of the same screen under the brand document
(from `/tmp/theme-brand/`); `-after` is this work. All full-size PNG.

## By item

1. Prominent buttons in dark mode (the label is now the ink, not white)
   - `start-chooser-dark-brand-{before,after}.png`: "Normal (Recommended)"
   - `standalone-dark-brand-{before,after}.png`: "Pair a Mac"
   - `whats-new-dark-brand-{before,after}.png`: "Continue"
   - `controls-dark-brand-after.png`: enabled, disabled and destructive
2. Section headers and footers
   - `controls-{light,dark}-brand-after.png`: "Themed header" is styled by the new
     modifier, "System header" is left to the system, for comparison
   - `controls-{light,dark}-default-after.png`: the same under the default document,
     where the two sections draw alike
3. Text the system draws
   - `controls-light-brand-after.png`: a large navigation title and a segmented control
   - `controls-inline-light-brand-after.png`: an inline title
   - `standalone-{light,dark}-brand-{before,after}.png`: the "No Paired Mac" empty state
   - `controls-empty-light-{brand,default}-after.png`: a plain empty state
5. The serif
   - `whats-new-{light,dark}-brand-{before,after}.png`: the title at 36 points
6. Icons
   - `session-list-{light,dark}-brand-{before,after}.png`: the machine icons

Item 4 (the composer's placeholder following a switch) has no picture: the composer
is not on a signed-out screen.

## Other

- `work/`: build and capture scripts, logs, `sections.py` (the script that rewrote the
  section headers and footers), and the pixel-band tool used to read the system's sizes.
- The default-document reference screens are in `/tmp/theme-ref/brand-fixes/`, compared
  against `~/.ripul/theme-reference/baseline`.

content.text:
Yes. Every screen in the iPhone and Catalyst apps, and the chat they show, now takes its fonts and colours from theme tokens. I checked the counts just now.

**Native (SDK and app)**
- Zero direct fonts or colours left, down from about 3,240.
- All ten streams are marked finished, so the build fails if anyone adds one.
- 189 places use a system colour through the token layer because no role fits yet, and 70 are marked exempt as data, such as a provider's or a chat's own colour.

**Web chat**
- Zero colour or typeface literals in the files the app's chat draws.
- 581 lines are marked exempt (syntax colours, debug overlays, model colours).

**What tokens do not reach**
- **Things the system draws.** Navigation titles, segmented controls, empty states and prominent button labels are now themed by other means. Menu values, alerts, menus, swipe actions and search fields still are not.
- **The Mac host's own screens,** the widgets and the Live Activity: left out on purpose.
- **Customer-themed content** (CMS blocks) and web surfaces the apps don't show, such as admin and the workflow designer.
- **Mac Catalyst presentations.** Sheets and popovers there do not take a themed accent yet; that item was not done.

**Since last night**
The native fix agent finished its report: all six fixes are on your phone, and the normal theme's reference screens still match the baseline. Its first run caught a real change (machine icons shifted in dark mode) and it fixed that before shipping.

Two things it could not look at on a signed-out simulator, so they are untested until you see them: Settings' section headers, and the composer's placeholder following a theme switch.

input.task:
You are closing a gap in Ripul's theming work, and then putting the result on the owner's iPhone. Read this whole brief before starting.

THE REPORT
Peter, whose product this is, opened the View Explorer in Ripul's own iPhone app this morning, selected an element, and under "Appearance" got "no token provider registered". The element was the top bar's leading button on the Agents screen:
  Type: UIPlatformGlassInteractionView
  Identifier: AgentScreen.topBar.leadingButton
  View controller: NavigationStackHostingController<AnyView>
  Frame in the host window (points): x=12, y=66, width=44, height=44
His phone is on the brand theme (`theme/ripul-theme-brand.json`), build 202610101948.

WHY IT SAYS THAT
Yesterday about 5,000 call sites in the SDK and the app were moved onto theme accessors (`.font(.ripul(.body))`, `.foregroundStyle(.ripul(.textSecondary))`, `Color.ripul(.accent)`, `.font(.ripulIcon(...))`), backed by a base vocabulary in `ripul-ios-sdk/Sources/RipulAgent/ThemeCore/`. The View Explorer was never connected to it. Its Appearance section (`InspectorTokenSection` in `ViewInspectorOverlay.swift`, near line 2114) asks `RipulTokenInspector.provider` for the bindings of the selected `UIView` (`RipulTokenInspection.swift`). That provider is the older host-engine mechanism: WAC registers one, and Ripul's app registers none except a UI-test fixture (`InspectorAppearanceTestProvider` in `ripul-native-app/iOS/RipulAppApp.swift`).

THE GOAL
In Ripul's own app, selecting an element in the View Explorer shows the theme tokens that style it: the colour roles and the type roles, each with what it resolves to now (a swatch, or a face and size) and whether that comes from the theme document or is the default. It must work for SwiftUI screens, which is nearly all of them, and it must be automatic.

THE HARD PART, AND THE RULE THAT GOVERNS IT
The explorer inspects UIKit views. SwiftUI draws into layers, so the view Peter tapped holds no colour or font to read back. `RipulTokenInspection.swift` already says so, and offers `.uiKitIdentifier(_:tokenColors:)`, a stamp on which a call site DECLARES its token colours. Nobody declares any, and asking 5,000 call sites to is exactly what Peter has ruled out: read `.ripul/memories/feedback_generalizable_native_theme_strategies.md`. One app-wide hook; no per-element registration; general strategies that work in any app using the SDK; where identity cannot be established, say so plainly in the explorer and do not guess.
So the provider has to learn, by itself, which tokens each identified element was drawn with. Two ways I can see; measure before choosing, and a mix is fine:
- At run time. A colour accessor's style is resolved with the environment in hand, and the identifier stamp could put the element's identifier into the environment of the content it marks, so resolving a role could record "this element used this role". Fonts have no such hook, so this alone does not cover type.
- At build time. The check and rewrite scripts in `ripul-native-app/scripts/` already recognise every accessor form. A script could read each `.uiKitIdentifier("…")` and the accessors in the view expression it belongs to, and write a map from identifier to tokens that the app bundles and the provider looks up. It covers fonts and colours alike, but only where an identifier is stamped, and only for apps that run the script.
Where the selected view has no identifier of its own, use the nearest identified ancestor and say that is what you did.

READ FIRST
- `ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md`, whole, and the files in `ThemeCore/`.
- `RipulTokenInspection.swift`, the Appearance section of `ViewInspectorOverlay.swift`, `ElementColours.swift`, `ElementText.swift`, and how the explorer's probe reports a selection (`RipulViewExplorer.swift`; the device tools include an explorer probe that returns the readout as text).
- How WAC's provider answers the same question, for the shape of a good answer: `~/Documents/WAC_ios_final-shift-rate-templates` (read only; change nothing there), and `.ripul/memories/` entries on the view explorer's provider and automatic label themes.
- docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.md: Decision 4, Foundation (F4, on what the theme editor cannot yet edit) and "The brand theme".
- ripul_guide topics `plans`, `trains`, `devices`.
- Your plan task is t_ca923c36852f: mark it doing now with planTaskStatus, write to its note as you go, and mark it done at the end with your report. Agent messages get lost when the host reloads; the plan's log is the record.

WHAT TO DELIVER
1. A provider for the base vocabulary, in the SDK, registered so that Ripul's app has one without a line per screen. It must not take over an app that registers its own (WAC): decide how the two coexist and say so.

entries.name: mcp__ripul_tools__device_explorer_probe
entries.description: Read the user's current View Explorer highlight, or highlight an app element at a screen coordinate. Omit both x and y to read the current selection without moving the reticule, reselecting, pressing, or opening the explorer. Reports isOpen and hasSelection, plus the selected element's text, label, identifier, frame and source readout when available. Supply both x and y to move the reticule and report what it resolves — the selected element, the element a tap would actually drive (they differ more often than you'd think), whether they diverge, and the readout verbatim. Optionally fire, which presses through the identical path a human tap takes and returns via/activated/trace. Coordinates are window-space, the same frames inspect_screen reports. With coordinates, automatically opens View Explorer if it is closed; no manual launch is needed. Omit fire or set it to false to highlight without pressing. Fire requires coordinates. This is the ONLY way to test point-based resolution; tap_element addresses by predicate and exercises a different path entirely. Runs on a remote device. Call device_list_targets to discover devices and their capabilities; pass device to select one.

device.description: Optional. Target a specific connected REMOTE device by its handle (e.g. "iphone-c603") — the value returned as `_device` on a previous result, and the only form guaranteed unique. A display name also works when it matches exactly one device; if it matches several the call fails and lists the handles. If omitted, this chat's working device is used (see device_list_targets); a chat without one uses the only connected device, and several connected devices fail. A device another agent holds refuses the call.

fire.description: Also press what resolves (default false). Requires both x and y; never fires in read mode.

x.description: Window-space x. Supply with y to move the highlight; omit both to read the current selection.

y.description: Window-space y. Supply with x to move the highlight; omit both to read the current selection.

[Agent reply · from "Theme: View Explorer shows an element's tokens" (cli_4169bfb7-6788-4d64-8cce-078803d6a963) · Claude Code · claude-cli-raw-opus · hop 2/8 · re agentmsg_1791701399502_8ug8dcfh3]
The View Explorer now names the theme tokens of a selected element, and build **202610110823** (commit `d35794bec`) is installed and verified on Peter's iPhone. Two of the six proving elements were not read on screen by themselves: a sidebar row and the prominent button.

`main` is at `929ab9a7b`, which adds only lint marks and a memory file. I did not relaunch the phone for it because Peter had picked it up (it rotated to landscape mid-test).

## How the provider learns an element's tokens

It learns at build time, from the source.

- **The map.** `ripul-native-app/scripts/theme_usage_map.py` reads every `.uiKitIdentifier("…")` and `.accessibilityIdentifier("…")` and the accessors in the view expression it ends. It finds four kinds:
  - accessors written on the element itself;
  - ones inherited from an enclosing `.font`, `.foregroundStyle` or `.tint` in the same function;
  - ones reached through a `Font` or `Color` property or a local `let`;
  - ones inside a view the expression names, two steps deep.
- **The bundle.** The Debug app build writes the result into the app as `ripul-theme-usage.json`. This is a new pre-build phase in `project.yml` and it cannot fail a build.
- **The provider.** `RipulBaseTokenProvider` in the SDK looks the identifier up and resolves each token against the live theme. Nothing registers it and no call site declares anything.
- **Coexistence with WAC.** A host's own provider is asked first and its answer stands alone. The base provider answers only where the host says nothing, and inside such a host it answers from the map only.

I chose build time because `Font.ripul` returns a plain `Font` and the Color form has no environment, so only the style form could record itself at run time. The source covers fonts and colours alike. Nothing is added to an accessor or a stamp, so the cost in a scrolling list is nil. Run-time recording was not built.

Measured on `main`: 1,529 stamps, 40 with the identifier in a variable, 875 naming at least one token, 3 seconds a run, 556 KB bundled.

## The readouts

These are the `appearance:` lines of the explorer's text readout. The first three are from Peter's phone on the brand document.

**1. The element Peter tapped** (probed at 34, 88). In list mode its identifier is `GlassTopBar.leadingButton`; `AgentScreen.topBar.leadingButton` is the same button inside a chat and has the same two tokens in the map.
```
Foreground: ripul.text, system:label · default [#FFFFFF]
Font: symbol size, 18 pt semibold · never themed
Written in: GlassTopBar.swift:491
```

**2. Session row title**
```
Font (in titleFont, one of several): caption, Archivo 12 pt semibold · family from the theme document
Font (in titleFont, one of several): body, Archivo 17 pt in a weight chosen at run time · family from the theme document
Written in: UnifiedSessionRow.swift:492
```

**3. Detail line** (the project name)
```
Foreground: ripul.textSecondary, system:secondaryLabel · default [#EBEBF5]
Font (in detailFont, one of several): caption2, Archivo 11 pt · family from the theme document
Font (in detailFont, one of several): caption, Archivo 12 pt · family from the theme document
Written in: UnifiedSessionRow.swift:573
```

**4. Navigation title, drawn by UIKit** (Duo simulator, controls fixture, brand document)
```
Font (read from the view): largeTitle bold, Archivo 34 pt · family from the theme document · same face and size as this role
Font set by: the theme, through UIKit's appearance settings for navigation titles
Text colour (read from the view): ripul.text, system:label · default · the same colour as this role [#000000]
```
Under the default document the same title reads `title bold, .AppleSystemUIFont 28 pt · default` and `Font set by: the system: a theme that names a text family restyles navigation titles`.

**5. Section header** (same fixture). The header has no identifier of its own, so the explorer says whose tokens it is showing:
```
Tokens shown for: ThemeControlsFixture, the identified element this view is a part of: the part has no identifier of its own, so which of these it uses is not known
Section header font (in form): headline, Archivo 17 pt semibold · family from the theme document
```

**6. Prominent button**, as lines of that same container readout:
```
Button fill (in form): ripul.accent, #1F6F70 light, #62B9B4 dark · theme document, through the window's tint [#1F6F70]
Button label (in form): ripul.onAccent, #FFFFFF light, #23253A dark · theme document [#FFFFFF]
```

## Not proved on screen

- **A sidebar row.** The sidebar's nav rows take their identifier from a variable, so they are not in the map. `SidebarView.nav.machineSection.name` is in the map (body font, `ripul.text` inherited), but I could not read it on screen. The Duo's wide layout has no sidebar, a signed-out simulator is not reachable by the device tools, and Peter was using his phone.
- **The prominent button by itself.** In the fixture the explorer's own identity named a screen covered by the fixture (`SolutionManagement.billing`), and the tokens followed that identity. This happens where one screen is drawn over another in the same window. It is a fault in the explorer's identity resolution and is not fixed here.

## What it cannot name, and what it says

| Situation | The explorer says |
|---|---|
| No identifier, and nothing identified around it | "This view has no identifier and nothing identified is around it… Give the element .uiKitIdentifier("Screen.part") and rebuild." |
| Identifier not in the map | "<id> is not in this build's theme usage map: the identifier is set outside the sources the map reads (in UIKit, from a variable, or in another package)…" |
| In the map, but no token | "<id> (File.swift:n) names no theme token in its own source: its colours and fonts come from a parameter, from the view that contains it, or from the system." |
| The build has no map | Says so, and that the app's build writes it. |
| A font or colour that is not a token | Listed as "not a theme token" with its source, for example the model name's colour: `modelIdentity?.color ?? providerColor`. |

It also cannot see a colour passed in as a parameter or a font set by a caller in another type. Where the code chooses between roles, each is listed as "one of several". The map is in Debug builds only.

## Checks

- **SDK theme tests:** 32 of 32 pass (21 existing, 11 new).
- **`check_theme_tokens.py`:** zero.
- **Rewrite lint** over my commits: passes.
- **SDK builds:** iOS simulator (the `--triple` form) and macOS both complete.
- **App:** compiled for the simulator and archived for the device by the ship scripts.
- **WAC:** build succeeded for v3 `e21efc8b1` in a `/tmp` worktree against the local SDK at `96fa77b56` (arm64 simulator, Debug; worktree removed). It was not rerun after the four later commits, which change only the provider's internals, a defaulted parameter and the dev-tools list.
- **Default document:** nothing touches an accessor, a stamp or a view. I did not compare against the reference screens.

## Other changes

- Ripul's own app now offers `explorer_probe` to device tools. It did not before, so the readout could not be read as text.
- The Duo simulator was switched to the brand document for two readouts and put back on `ripul-theme`.
- I did not commit `docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.plan.jsonl` and `.review.md`: they were already modified by other sessions when I started. My task notes are in that uncommitted log.

## Left for editing a token from the explorer

Nothing is editable yet: the rows are read-only and `remap` returns nil. Editing needs:

1. An editor for a base role that can write a light and dark pair and choose a system colour (Foundation F4).
2. A type-role editor.
3. Somewhere to keep the edit: the app loads a bundled document and has no draft for it.

Also worth doing: give the sidebar's rows literal identifiers, record the style form at run time to say which of "one of several" is live, and fix the covered-screen identity fault.

content.text:
Both: the editing screens are mostly supplied by the SDK, and WAC wraps them in its own shell and supplies everything that is specific to WAC.

**From the SDK**
- **The engine:** resolving tokens, the style cascade, applying a change live and repainting.
- **The editing screens:** the colours screen (palette, roles, component tokens), the components and style screens, the style library, per-screen scopes and overrides, and the style picker with live preview.
- **The explorer's remap sheet:** what opens when you double-tap an element in the View Explorer.
- **Element-level edits:** colour overrides for one element, and the text library for label and tab wording.
- **Publishing:** the draft, review-and-publish, and the hosted theme document.

**WAC's own**
- **The vocabulary:** the token names, roles, palette, and which style kinds exist with which knobs. WAC registers these with the engine at launch.
- **The document and its typed model:** about 2,900 lines that own WAC's theme file, including the parts the engine never sees.
- **The editor's shell:** the landing screen and navigation, plus WAC-specific previews (masthead, hub row, content card, panel, field).
- **Typography and metrics:** the font-family picker and the size settings. The engine has no fonts, so this part is entirely WAC's.
- **The token provider:** the piece that tells the explorer which tokens style a view.

By size, WAC's own theme code is about 4,300 lines in four files, against about 6,100 lines of theme code in the SDK.

**What that means for Ripul.** Those SDK screens edit a host's vocabulary in the older engine. Ripul's new tokens live in a separate base vocabulary that the screens do not know about, and they could not edit it safely anyway: they write a single colour where Ripul needs a light and dark pair, and they have no font editing. So editing Ripul's theme needs SDK work first (a pair-aware colour editor, a type editor, somewhere to keep a draft) and then only a thin Ripul shell. Done in the SDK, WAC could use the type editor too.

message.content: I am getting a little concerned now , I wanted the theme system to be a key value of the sdk , yet applying it to our app , has been tough , or do I have that wrong ?

content.text:
You have it half right. It was tough, and the reason matters for the SDK: the theme system as it stood did not fit an app like ours.

**Why it was hard**

- **The engine came from WAC.** WAC is a light-only UIKit app. Ours is SwiftUI, follows light and dark, and had to keep the system look by default. The engine had no fonts, one value per colour, nothing a SwiftUI view could read, and an explorer that only sees UIKit colours.
- **We were retrofitting.** About 5,000 places set their own font or colour. That part was actually fast, around three hours, once the rewrite script, lint and check existed.

So most of yesterday was not "applying the SDK's theme system". It was building the half the SDK lacked.

**What the SDK gained**

It now has the SwiftUI layer: accessors, fonts, light and dark, live repaint, a root modifier, restyling of system-drawn titles, and an explorer that names tokens with no registration. A SwiftUI customer would have hit the same wall we did; better that we hit it first.

**What stops me calling it a key value yet**

1. **There are now two theme systems in the SDK.** WAC uses the older engine, where the host defines its own tokens. Ripul uses a new base layer with a fixed set of about 15 colour roles and 14 type roles. They have different documents, and the editor only understands the older one.
2. **The editor cannot edit the new tokens.** "Tap an element, change it, publish" works in WAC and not in Ripul.
3. **The migration tools are not in the SDK.** The rewrite script, lint, check and usage map live in our app's scripts folder and carry our file layout. A customer gets none of them.
4. **Some of the screen is out of reach.** Grouped lists, alerts, menus and parts of Catalyst follow no theme, and that is SwiftUI's limit as much as ours.

**What I'd do**

Decide whether the two systems become one, then prove the path on an app that is not ours or WAC: add the SDK, wrap the root, run the script, write a theme, edit it in the explorer. The Sandsend app being built in another chat would be a fair test. If that takes an afternoon, it is a real SDK value; if it takes what yesterday took, it is not yet.

python3 - <<'PYEOF'
p='docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.md'
s=open(p).read()
marker='## The vocabulary\n'
assert s.count(marker)==1
new='''### 9. One theme system going forward

Decided by Peter on 11 October 2026, after the migration showed that the SDK now holds two theme systems: "I don't mind the WAC app carrying a legacy for a while as long as moving forward it is clean."

- **The base layer is the SDK's theme system.** That is `RipulTheme`, the accessors, the theme document, the root, the usage map and the provider built on it. Everything new is built on it and on nothing else.
- **The older engine is legacy.** `RipulThemeEngine`, its vocabulary registration and its editing screens stay as they are for WAC. They take fixes, not features, and nothing new may depend on them. The SDK's documents say so.
- **No bridges from the new to the old.** Ripul's roles do not go into a host's document, and the new layer reads nothing from the older engine. The reserved `ripul` key in a host's document stays reserved and unread (decision 4).
- **Editing is built new.** An editor for the base layer (light and dark pairs, system colours, type roles, a draft, publishing) is written for it, reusing only what is already general, such as hosting and the publish review. The older screens are not bent to fit.
- **WAC moves later, as its own piece of work,** by a mapping from its vocabulary. Until then it runs the legacy engine unchanged.

Two things have to be settled for the forward path to be clean for an app that is not ours. Neither is built:

- **A host's own tokens.** The base layer has a fixed set of roles. A customer's app, and WAC when it moves, need to add their own.
- **The tools travel with the SDK.** The rewrite script, the lint, the check and the usage map live in this app's scripts folder and carry its file layout.

'''
s=s.replace(marker,new+marker)
open(p,'w').write(s)
PYEOF
cat > .ripul/memories/project_theme_one_system_going_forward.md <<'EOF'
---
name: theme-one-system-going-forward
description: "Peter's decision of 11 Oct 2026: the SDK's new base theme layer (RipulTheme, accessors) is the theme system going forward; the older RipulThemeEngine is legacy that WAC carries; build nothing new on it"
metadata:
  type: project
  scope: repo
  repo: ripul
  scope_also: repo:wac-ios
---

After the theme migration of 10 October 2026 the SDK held two theme systems: the older engine lifted from WAC (`RipulThemeEngine`: a host registers its own vocabulary, UIKit colour tagging, the editing and publishing screens) and the new base layer built for Ripul's SwiftUI app (`RipulTheme` in `ThemeCore/`: fixed roles, accessors, light and dark, fonts, live repaint, the usage map and `RipulBaseTokenProvider`). I told Peter this was the main thing standing between the theme system and being a real SDK value. His decision, 11 October 2026, in the chat "Design alignment": "I don't mind the WAC app carrying a legacy for a while as long as moving forward it is clean."

**Why:** he wants the theme system to be a key value of the SDK. Applying the older engine to our own app was hard because it fits the UIKit, light-only app it came from, so the forward path has to be the layer that fits SwiftUI apps, kept free of the old one.

**How to apply:**
- Build every new theme feature on the base layer only: editing, the explorer, publishing a base document, migration tools.
- Treat `RipulThemeEngine`, its vocabulary registration and its editor screens (`Theme*.swift` outside `ThemeCore/`) as legacy: fixes only, no features, no new dependents. Do not extend the old editor to edit base roles; write the base layer's editor new, reusing only what is already general (hosting, the publish review).
- No bridges from new to old: nothing of the base layer goes into a host's own palette or roles maps, and the reserved `ripul` key in a host document stays unread.
- WAC stays on the legacy engine unchanged until it is moved as its own piece of work. Do not break it, and do not migrate it as a side effect.
- Still open and not built (my reading of what "clean" needs, not his words): a host adding its own roles to the base layer, and shipping the rewrite script, lint, check and usage map with the SDK and without Ripul's file layout.

The decision is recorded as Decision 9 in `docs/plans/theme-aware-codebase.md`. See [[theme-framework-sdk-lift]] for how the older engine got into the SDK, and `ripul-ios-sdk/docs/theming.md` for the base layer's contract.
EOF

After the theme migration of 10 October 2026 the SDK held two theme systems: the older engine lifted from WAC (`RipulThemeEngine`: a host registers its own vocabulary, UIKit colour tagging, the editing and publishing screens) and the new base layer built for Ripul's SwiftUI app (`RipulTheme` in `ThemeCore/`: fixed roles, accessors, light and dark, fonts, live repaint, the usage map and `RipulBaseTokenProvider`). Understood, and I've recorded it as the rule: the new layer is the SDK's theme system, and the older engine is WAC's legacy. It is Decision 9 in the plan, and a shared memory so other agents hold to it.

**What "clean going forward" means in practice**

2. **The tools travel with the SDK.** The rewrite script, lint, check and usage map sit in our app's scripts folder and carry our file layout.

**The explorer fix landed while we talked.** I probed your top-bar button on your phone again. #!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# release-public.sh — Publish the monorepo RipulAgent SDK to the public
# ripulio/ripul-ios-sdk repo as a clean, one-way mirror + version tag.
#
# The monorepo copy (this script's parent dir) is the source of truth. Histories
# between the two repos diverged long ago, so we do NOT merge — we overwrite the
# public repo's working tree with the monorepo SDK (rsync --delete), commit, and
# tag vX.Y.Z. The push to GitHub happens ONLY with --push (outward-facing step).
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/release-public.sh 0.1.0           # stage locally (mirror + commit + tag), no push
#   scripts/release-public.sh 0.1.0 --push    # also push commit + tag to origin
#
# Env:
#   RIPUL_PUBLIC_SDK   path to the public repo clone
#                      (default: $HOME/Documents/ripul-ios-sdk)
set -euo pipefail

VERSION="${1:-}"
PUSH=""
[ "${2:-}" = "--push" ] && PUSH=1

SRC="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"          # monorepo SDK root
DEST="${RIPUL_PUBLIC_SDK:-$HOME/Documents/ripul-ios-sdk}"        # public repo clone
REMOTE_NAME="origin"
TAG="v${VERSION}"

die() { echo "❌ $*" >&2; exit 1; }

[ -n "$VERSION" ] || die "usage: $0 <version> [--push]   e.g. $0 0.1.0"
echo "$VERSION" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' \
  || die "version must be semver X.Y.Z (got: $VERSION)"
[ -d "$SRC/Sources/RipulAgent" ] || die "source SDK not found at $SRC/Sources/RipulAgent"
[ -d "$DEST/.git" ]              || die "public repo clone not found at $DEST (set RIPUL_PUBLIC_SDK)"

echo "▶ Source (monorepo): $SRC"
echo "▶ Dest   (public):   $DEST"
echo "▶ Version:           $TAG"
echo

# Public clone must be clean and not already tagged at this version.
git -C "$DEST" diff --quiet && git -C "$DEST" diff --cached --quiet \
  || die "public repo has uncommitted changes — clean it first"
git -C "$DEST" fetch "$REMOTE_NAME" --tags --quiet || true
if git -C "$DEST" rev-parse --verify "refs/tags/$TAG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  die "tag $TAG already exists — bump the version"
fi

# Stamp the marketing version into the SDK source, so the View Explorer's
# `sdk: …` line reports the release that is actually running on the device.
# Hand-bumping this drifted (it sat at 0.5.8 through the whole 0.6/0.7 series,
# making every element paste misreport the build), so the release owns it.
# Committed in the MONOREPO — the source of truth — before the dirty check
# below, so the tag and the constant can never disagree.
VERSION_FILE="$SRC/Sources/RipulAgent/ViewInspectorOverlay.swift"
CURRENT_VERSION="$(sed -n 's/^let ripulSDKVersion = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' "$VERSION_FILE")"
[ -n "$CURRENT_VERSION" ] || die "could not read ripulSDKVersion from $VERSION_FILE"
if [ "$CURRENT_VERSION" != "$VERSION" ]; then
  sed -i '' "s/^let ripulSDKVersion = \".*\"\$/let ripulSDKVersion = \"$VERSION\"/" "$VERSION_FILE"
...
