=== feedback_sdk_release_from_clean_worktree.md
---
name: feedback_sdk_release_from_clean_worktree
description: "Publish an SDK tag from a detached worktree at HEAD when the monorepo SDK tree is dirty with another agent's WIP — never ALLOW_DIRTY=1, never stash"
metadata:
  type: feedback
  scope: repo
  repo: ripul
---

`ripul-ios-sdk/scripts/release-public.sh` refuses a dirty `Sources`/`Package.swift`
tree because rsync copies the WORKING TREE, so another agent's in-flight edits ride
into the public tag (this already shipped an in-flight AgentScreen port as v0.4.14).
In this repo the SDK tree is dirty with foreign work most of the time.

**Do not** reach for `ALLOW_DIRTY=1`, and do not stash. Publish from a clean
detached worktree at the commit you actually want:

```bash
# 1. Stamp + commit the new version in MAIN first — the script's own stamp step
#    would commit to the worktree's detached HEAD and be lost.
sed -i '' 's/^let ripulSDKVersion = ".*"$/let ripulSDKVersion = "X.Y.Z"/' \
  ripul-ios-sdk/Sources/RipulAgent/ViewInspectorOverlay.swift
git commit -m "chore(sdk): stamp ripulSDKVersion X.Y.Z" && git push

# 2. Release from a clean checkout of that commit.
git worktree add --detach /tmp/ripul-sdk-release-X.Y.Z HEAD
cd /tmp/ripul-sdk-release-X.Y.Z/ripul-ios-sdk && bash scripts/release-public.sh X.Y.Z --push
cd - && git worktree remove /tmp/ripul-sdk-release-X.Y.Z --force   # ALWAYS remove it
```

=== feedback_sdk_release_after_all_edits.md
---
name: feedback_sdk_release_after_all_edits
description: Cut the ripul-ios-sdk tag only AFTER every SDK edit for the change is done — a late edit strands WAC on a tag without it
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 3a38c80e-bb09-43b5-98aa-662a86f4f64a
  modified: 2026-07-28T08:39:43.264Z
  scope: repo
  repo: ripul
  scope_also: repo:wac-ios
---

`release-public.sh vX.Y.Z --push` snapshots the SDK working tree at that moment. Any SDK
edit made *after* the tag — even one that builds clean locally — is NOT in the tag WAC
pins, so WAC fails with `cannot find type 'X' in scope` even though the symbol exists in
the monorepo.

Hit 2026-07-28: released 0.5.40, then made `RipulTokenNode`/`RipulTokenNodeScreen` public
so WAC's scope trees could share the builder. Local SDK build passed (it compiles the
monorepo copy); WAC's build failed against the 0.5.40 tag. Cost a full WAC rebuild cycle.

**Why:** the local `swift build`/`xcodebuild` of the SDK proves nothing about what WAC
sees — WAC resolves the PUBLIC repo at the pinned tag, a separate checkout.

**How to apply:** finish every SDK edit for the change (including access-level widening
discovered while wiring the host) → build SDK → *then* release + bump the pin. If a host
build fails on a missing SDK symbol, check `git log v<pinned>..HEAD -- ripul-ios-sdk/`
before debugging the host. See [[project_wac_consumes_sdk_as_pinned_public_package]].

v0.7.168
v0.7.169

== monorepo tree
?? HANDOVER-permission-allowlist.md
fi

# Concurrency guard: refuse to mirror a DIRTY monorepo tree. The rsync below copies
# the working tree, so uncommitted edits and untracked files ride into the tag —
# and several agents work in this tree concurrently (v0.4.14 shipped an in-flight
# AgentScreen port to WAC this way). Commit (or set aside) foreign work first, or
# pass ALLOW_DIRTY=1 when you really mean it.
if [ "${ALLOW_DIRTY:-}" != "1" ]; then
  dirty="$(git -C "$SRC" status --porcelain -- Sources Package.swift)"
  [ -z "$dirty" ] || die "monorepo SDK tree is dirty — refusing to scoop uncommitted work into $TAG:
$dirty
(commit it, or override with ALLOW_DIRTY=1)"
fi

# Guardrail: no `import Charts`. A host that already has a module named Charts (WAC links
# the danielgindi Charts pod under that name) shadows Apple's framework at link time, so the
# SDK fails to LINK in that host — v0.7.144 shipped that way and WAC could not take it.
if grep -rnE '^[[:space:]]*import[[:space:]]+Charts([[:space:]]|$)' "$SRC/Sources" 2>/dev/null; then
  die "the SDK imports Charts (see above) — hosts with a Charts pod cannot link it; draw the chart with SwiftUI shapes"
fi

# One-way mirror: make the public tree identical to the monorepo SDK, minus VCS
# and build artifacts. Excluded paths are also protected from --delete on DEST.

input.task:
You are the developer of Sandsend Retreats, a small SwiftUI iPhone app (this repository; read its CLAUDE.md first). You are about to adopt the theme system of the Ripul SDK, which this app already links. This is an experiment, and the experiment is about you: Peter, who owns both this app and the SDK, wants to know exactly how much work the SDK's theme system costs a host app. His goal is that the host does the bare minimum and the SDK carries the complexity. So the most valuable thing you produce is not a themed app. It is an honest, itemised account of everything you had to do, know, guess or work around.

THE RULE THAT MAKES THE MEASUREMENT HONEST
You may use only what a host developer gets:
- the public SDK package at v0.7.170 (https://github.com/ripulio/ripul-ios-sdk), which carries the theme layer for the first time. Its source and its `docs/` folder arrive in the package checkout; `docs/theming.md` is the theme system's contract;
- the `ripul_guide` tool (topics `sdk`, `devices`, `trains`, `plans`);
- this repository.
You may NOT learn from the SDK's home repository at ~/Documents/ripul: not its app, its scripts, its plans or its memories. It is on this disk and it has every answer, which is exactly why reading it would spoil the test. If you reach a point where you cannot go on without it, stop, write down precisely what you needed and why the package did not give it to you, and only then look. Each such moment is a headline finding. Do not change the SDK either: if it lacks something, work around it in this app and count the workaround.

WHAT TO DO TO THE APP
On a branch named `theme-trial` (never commit this to `main`; push the branch):
1. Take SDK 0.7.170 (the pin is `exactVersion` in project.yml).
2. Make every screen take its fonts and colours from the theme, with nothing looking different under the default theme.
3. Give the app a brand theme that carries the look of its website, www.sandsendretreats.com, and of its install page (a serif, paper and navy; the install page's styles are described in this repo's CLAUDE.md). Bundle whatever fonts that needs, with their licences.
4. Make the theme switchable at run time between the default and the brand, the way theming.md describes.
5. In a Debug build, the Ripul View Explorer should name the theme tokens that style an element you select.
6. Light and dark both right.
Today every use of the SDK in this app is inside `#if DEBUG`; the SDK is a developer tool here. Theming puts SDK calls into production code. Treat that as part of what you are measuring: what it does to a Release build (size before and after, build time, anything a store build would have to worry about).

THE LEDGER (keep it as you go, not from memory afterwards)
For every step you take, one row:
- what you did and why it was needed;
- the lines you added, changed and removed in this repository, and in which files (from git, not estimated);
- how long it took, from the clock (note a timestamp when you start and finish each step);
- where the knowledge came from: theming.md, the SDK's source, the guide, a guess that worked, a guess that failed, or the forbidden repository;
- whether the host should have had to do this at all, and if not, what the SDK would have to do for it to disappear.
Sort the work into kinds, because Peter will ask for totals of each: one-off setup; edits to call sites that a tool could have made; edits that needed a human decision; writing the theme document; fonts; build-system changes; workarounds for something the SDK lacks; time lost to something that did not work or was not documented.

THE LAST STEP
Put the trial build on Peter's iPhone by direct install, as this repo's CLAUDE.md describes for his phone. Do not publish it to the public install page (`scripts/ship_ota.py`): this is a trial on a branch. Leave the app on the brand theme so that is what he sees when he opens it. Peter judges work by what is on his phone; do not stop at "committed".

THE READOUT
Write it to `/Users/petermaude/Documents/ripul/docs/plans/sdk-theme-host-burden.md` (writing that one file there is allowed; reading the rest of that repository is not). It will be read on a phone, so lead with the answer. Sections, with these `##` headings:
- `## The answer`: in five lines or fewer, what it cost a host today: the minutes, the lines, the number of things you had to know that the package did not tell you.
- `## The ledger`: the table of steps, then the totals by kind.
- `## What did not work`: every dead end, every undocumented requirement, every time you needed the SDK's source or the forbidden repository.
- `## What the host should have had to do`: your view, as the host, of the bare minimum. Be concrete: "add the package, name a theme file, nothing else" is the kind of statement wanted, with what stops it being true today for each item.
- `## Not measured`: what you did not check.
Commit that file in that repository by path (`git -C /Users/petermaude/Documents/ripul add docs/plans/sdk-theme-host-burden.md` then `git -C … commit -m "…" -- docs/plans/sdk-theme-host-burden.md`, then push). Many sessions share that repository's index, so never a bare commit there, and never stash or reset. Write a first version early and update it as you go: the host that runs these chats can lose your final message, and the file is the record.

Say for every figure whether you measured it or estimated it.
